Resume only after every pending ID is resolved. A resolved latest batch remains recorded context through later transitions and plain pauses; do not ask those questions again. Scope-changing answers follow the [replacement and rebind route](#record-and-resolve-decision-batches). When a plain pause names a human decision, ask it with your recommended default and wait for that answer before dependent work or resume.
- **Merge a named change:** handle a plain merge request as a repository action on the existing change, preserving its current review and authority requirements; do not create new intake merely to perform the merge.
- **Was it merged, is anything left, is it ready:** read the exact item status and inspect a current attempt when present before naming remaining review. For the agreed work still left, read the current attempt's `current_checkpoint`. It names the current brief's checkpoint; `continue` adds the exact `remaining_work` that brief records beyond that checkpoint, the same text focused completion discovery reports; `terminal` records no further checkpoint; `unreadable` leaves the remaining work unknown, not empty. Checkpoint acceptance does not change the current brief: until a rebind or a resume with a revised brief, a `checkpoint-accepted` verdict and `current_checkpoint` name the same accepted checkpoint, and only `remaining_work` is left. After that rebind or resume, `current_checkpoint` names the new checkpoint, unfinished until accepted, while the verdict still names the last accepted one. A terminal item has no current attempt. A `ready` verdict is a verified commissioned review of its named candidate; `reconcile-repository` means that review is recorded and repository disposition remains. When the human reports a rebase, squash merge or merge, resolve the intended target and run item-status operation `integration` before calling the earlier review insufficient because commit identities changed. `content-present` verifies that candidate's accepted diff at the returned local `target_revision`: say the review covered the original candidate and its reviewed content reached the target. It does not establish review of every surrounding commit. `content-not-present` and `no-change` are inconclusive; inspect changed content or selected historical evidence before naming a gap. A verified gap is in `main` but unreviewed, and you recommend review of that landed change. Unknown or conflicting coverage stays qualified, and remote identity stays observed or unverified. Merged work owing review is review work, not implementation in flight. Keep required current-subject commissioning and ready recording separate from historical narration.
- **Close, complete, or mark done:** first check that the human explicitly asked to close this item. If you fixed or implemented it yourself and they did not ask, report the change and where it landed, ask whether to close it, and stop. `close` applies to eligible live work without an attempt and to absorbed items eligible for `superseded`: an unresolved current planned replacement names an existing non-dropped item, every live dependent has moved to that item or its declared checkpoints, and any preserved attempt is paused or blocked. Superseded closure ends the preserved attempt and fences its authority without claiming successful completion; active or review attempts cannot close. Follow [the close procedure](#apply-a-transition) only through `pinboard_close`, whose `human_decision` carries the human's explicit close decision in their own words; if you do not have those words, ask and stop. Claude Code v2.1.199 or later asks the human to confirm every `pinboard_close` call; Codex and earlier Claude Code versions may not ask. Antigravity asks through Pinboard's PreToolUse `force_ask` decision, so the close is unavailable in headless `agy -p` runs; when that hook does not run, Antigravity's own approval settings decide. If the call is denied, report that the human must confirm the close and seek no other route. When the item has an attempt, read its current verdict and inspect that attempt. For successful completion, keep its normal evidence-backed review path. When the human reports integration, check the named target through the route above before describing any review still owed. If commissioned ready review is already recorded, say what it covered and reuse that valid review through the fresh completion contract when the agreed outcome and authorized disposition are satisfied. Changed commit identities alone do not require another review or another close confirmation. If completion refuses because work or evidence remains, report its actual accepted remaining work or missing current candidate, review, or evidence and follow the focused inspection. Preserve an eligible current review when read-only investigation or explicit retention settles existing scope, recording that decision separately from the bound brief, result and review. Closure authorizes no automatic candidate reconstruction or implementation launch. If the required record is missing, explain the review still owed and offer that route: completion requires a reviewer commissioned through `pinboard_review_job`, its ready verdict recorded with `record-ready`, and that reviewer's identity. Content presence alone cannot replace that record. Status-only requests authorize these reads and a reply, never completion or review commissioning. Never pause, block, defer, or resume work, or run the CLI `close`, to approximate a close or completion.
- **Fix, start, or implement a saved item now:** say in one sentence what will be produced and where it will land, ask only a question whose answer would change the result, with your recommendation, then follow [Prepare delegated attempts](#prepare-delegated-attempts). Do not edit or commit source for the item directly unless the human chooses to work outside Pinboard.

- for each attempt in review, its item-status `review_verdict` and `pinboard_attempt_inspect` with `reconciliation: null`: a valid `ready` verdict and `reconcile-repository` mean review is recorded, so gather the named repository observations and check reported integration before presenting any unresolved disposition. `review-subagent` means it waits for a reviewer;
- for each active attempt, `pinboard_attempt_authority` operation `status`—an active holder is a running worker, none means nobody is working on it; a preparation record cannot replace this read—and its item status `review_verdict`, where `returned-for-correction` means a correction is owed; when its `rebound_since_return` is true the return is history, and [replacement-brief recovery](#recover-after-a-brief-replacement) records a new return before correction;
- for each paused item, its `pinboard_item_status` operation `item` result, whose current `pause_reason` and any pending `decision_batch` say what it waits on;
- in Git, `git branch --no-merged <target>`. For an unmerged branch with no live item, find the items and attempts that own it with `pinboard_item_status` operation `branch`, then read the owning item's status; a terminal item's `closure` says when and by which action it closed, its recorded `outcome_evidence` says whether the human deliberately retained or deferred the unmerged change and where a kept experiment's scratch board is. Preserve that settled decision; product absence alone creates no new adoption choice. Present a landing choice only when it remains unresolved, and assess exact review coverage separately. For a live item whose branch is already merged, check whether a review covered it and whether `origin/<target>` contains the merge. `pinboard_item_status` operation `integration` with that `target` reports whether the item's reviewed candidate diff is `content-present` there, including after a rebase or squash merge; `content-not-present` does not prove the change is absent.

Default `$pinboard`, `/pinboard`, “where do we stand?”, “quick status”, and equivalent orientation questions to one complete same-revision overview traversal plus the focused reads that [the human's picture](#keep-the-humans-picture-current) requires; never call `pinboard_initiative` (`roadmap`) unless the user asks about initiatives or the roadmap. Keep the reply within [the shared policy’s ~150-word budget](#keep-the-humans-picture-current). Lead with what waits on the human, then work in progress (active, in-review, and paused items) with who acts next, then the immediate next ready items in saved order with dependency reasons. On a large board, list every item waiting on the human, every active/in-review/paused item, and the immediate next ready items, then give a count of the remaining ready, blocked, and deferred items rather than listing every item on the board; link the generated board page on the closing line for the full queue. Give each listed item one line of at most twelve words—the item, where it stands in the human's terms, and your default when it waits on them—and leave out facts you did not read. Those lines are the answer's open items, so a status answer has no `Still open:` line and asks at most one question. Link every mentioned item under the [readable-artifact rule](#match-detail-to-the-question). Intake candidates already appear in that order. The revision stamp is freshness evidence, not reply content. Read selected historical evidence or an earlier decision only when needed to substantiate a review claim or distinguish a settled choice from an open one; do not preload full history, project notes, GitHub, CI or delivery state for this default answer. Acquire no lease merely to explain the live picture.

Keep inspection, validation, repair, and project-export claims distinct. `pinboard_item_status` operation `item` and both `pinboard_item_definition` leaves read only the named item facts, the item leaf adding the current attempt's accepted brief by its reference; the item leaf also carries the current attempt's `branch`, a paused attempt's `pause_reason`, each current attempt's latest `decision_batch` with any recorded resolution, the current attempt's `review_verdict` and `current_checkpoint`, a terminal item's `closure`, and intake-time next action and notes only as labeled original context in `intake_context`. Item-status operation `branch` scans retained attempts for every item and attempt that recorded that exact branch; a branch recorded before a rebind is not found. Item-status operation `integration` with `item_id` and `target` reads only that item's reviewed candidate evidence and runs one read-only Git content check against the named local target without fetching. Use definition operation `current` for complete accepted fields and revision/digest identity, never a title or status substitute. Use operation `history` only when history is requested, with an explicit 1–100 limit and `before_revision: null` initially, continuing with the returned exclusive `next_before_revision` while it is non-null. These reads, like direct attempt- and preparation-authority status, need no lease.

`pinboard_attempt_inspect` reads one named attempt context and verifies its accepted brief. Its required nullable `reconciliation` is `null` for ordinary inspection, or the outer coordinator's target revision, exact integration relation, legal repository phase, and ordered source-checkout, shared-work-root, and git-metadata effect observations. For a favorably reviewed candidate, `null` returns the ordinary `reconcile-repository` continuation naming the observations needed next, and those observations then select one repository continuation; Pinboard never performs the repository or permission effect. Every nonterminal continuation carries the latest `decision_batch` and its recorded resolution when present; a paused continuation separately carries the current pause's recorded `pause_reason`. `pinboard_review_job` reads that attempt context, accepted brief, and current `result.md`; an optional caller-selected package adds the exact checkpoint history receipt and package artifact, and optional correction context adds the exact return receipt and current `review.md`, all in one focused read transaction. Review launch leaves may publish an immutable reviewer prompt, accept its artifact reference, and advance the ledger; the non-launching `record-ready` leaf verifies the exact attempt, candidate snapshot, accepted brief, result and review digests, independent reviewer, and favorable verdict, then publishes or reuses the canonical candidate review. Neither path mutates lifecycle, candidate state, attempt authority, repository files, or Git. `pinboard_parallel_preview` with explicit selected `item_ids` reads only those items, their direct launch constraints, and applicable authority; its explicit all-safe leaf is project-wide. Retained CLI `status`, `pinboard_actions`, and that all-safe preview each project one current SQLite snapshot; each bounded overview page selects compact rows in its own revision-bound snapshot without validating accepted artifacts or generated views. Use `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard validate` when integrity matters: it verifies the snapshot and accepted artifact bytes, validates each v2-linked checkpoint or reviewed-completion package against its historical receipt and immutable evidence, and reports generated-view drift as repairable warnings without repairing; `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard views rebuild` is that separate write. Use `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard export --json` only to materialize one strict `pinboard-project-export/v3` package of the supported project-facts subset from one snapshot and verified artifacts; it applies the same package validation, exposes valid checkpoint and completion packages as typed portable evidence beside their generic artifact entries, keeps authority local, and contacts no receiving tool.

End every compact overview with one short offer to expand the useful layers: recommendation and item context; completed decisions; delivery and CI; or full history. Make it a single line, either a natural sentence or, as the text fallback of the [question presentation](#match-detail-to-the-question), `Quick reply: 1 why next · 2 decisions · 3 delivery/CI · 4 full history`, never both. The same closing line of a status or task-list answer carries one link to the board page, using the `html` path from the overview's `board` object under the [readable-artifact rule](#match-detail-to-the-question); add no separate board section.

Do not invent slash commands for these follow-ups. `$pinboard` is an explicit entry point for invoking the skill in a new or unrelated context, where terse prompts such as `$pinboard quick status` or `$pinboard full history` are valid. It is not a required subcommand inside an ongoing pinboard conversation.

Fetch only the selected expansion:

- For a recommendation or deeper rationale, use the overview itself when it contains enough evidence. Otherwise read only the exact live item records that are plausible choices. Apply the ordering below only then.
- For completed decisions, read terminal item history only. Do not add GitHub or delivery checks.
- For delivery or CI, inspect Git and GitHub only. Do not reconstruct ledger history.
- For full history, say that the answer will be slower, then read the complete relevant ledger and accepted artifact context. Add delivery state only if the user includes it.

When an expansion needs several known project files or headings, plan their selected sizes with `pinboard_brief_sources` before loading their bodies: on Claude Code and Codex, read each non-overlapping emitted batch once; on Antigravity, read the planned sources through the Antigravity native-source procedure with native `read_file` using the plan's paths and line spans instead of calling `emit` or `emit-file`. For other known facts, use a bounded batch when the available tool supports it. If output truncates, continue at the first unread boundary without replaying returned content. Do not turn one requested layer into an exploratory command-per-item walk. If the user explicitly asks for a zero-tool or last-known answer, reuse the most recent overview from the current conversation and label it as not refreshed. Never present it as current. A requested expansion is not permission to preload the other layers.

This proportional behavior applies to mutation as well as status. After a successful command returns a revision-stamped receipt, do not run a redundant overview merely to confirm what the command already proved. Run broader verification only when the operation lacks a sufficient postcondition or the user asks for it.

## Bounded discovery

Known-item work starts with `pinboard_item_status` operation `item` and, when definition context is needed, `pinboard_item_definition` operation `current`. Known-attempt delivery, review and recovery start with exact attempt inspection and the phase's required authority/evidence reads. Do not add board-wide discovery to these focused routes.

For a board-wide question, call `pinboard_overview` with top-level exact `project_root`, `work_root`, `max_items` from 1 to 25, and `continuation: null`. Each `pinboard-overview/v8` page enforces at most that many rows and an 8000-byte complete SDK envelope, including duplicate text, arrays, metadata and continuation. Labels are prefixes of at most 160 characters, not complete titles. Dependency counts are counts, not omitted-target lists. These summaries grant no start, mutation, worker, preparation or review authority.

Keep the same roots and pass the returned `continuation` unchanged on the next call. Emit and consume one page at a time. Stop at null; only the accumulated sequence at that revision supports complete-board counts, absence claims or `pinboard_order.expected_order`. A stale or invalid continuation rejects unchanged: restart with null and discard the prior partial traversal. If traversal cannot finish, explicitly report partial coverage; never infer that unseen pauses, blockers or human decisions do not exist. Oversized row or metadata rejection leaves state unchanged and requires the named focused read or human diagnosis; never silently skip a row.

Read selected item status for full dependency reasons and targets, proposal origin, replacement cost, preparation, pauses and review facts; read its current definition for complete title, effect and unlock. Complete board-wide status still identifies every item waiting on the human and every active/review/paused item before summarizing the rest. Follow focused reads only for facts needed by that answer.

## Interpret the available actions

Translate executable actions into ordinary repository and product language; the exact action record serves execution only. Whenever the explanation names an item, decision, or evidence artifact with confirmed readable Markdown, apply the shared readable-artifact link rule.

When selecting work, explain:

1. the current product or repository trajectory;
2. what changed after the last accepted item;
3. which items are ready and why;
4. which items are blocked and the exact unresolved condition;
5. which ordering is mechanically determined by dependencies;
6. which choice genuinely requires human priority;
7. the recommended next item and why now.

When known intake or selected-item context shows several ready items sharing a first step or scarce resource, or each too small to justify its own start, review, publication and close, apply the shared policy’s [shared-phase suggestion](#match-detail-to-the-question) once: recommend one autonomous campaign item with each deliverable as a named checkpoint. Keep compact status read-only; use the overview or focused context already needed for the answer, without a broad discovery walk. The suggestion leaves saved order, dependencies, and human choice intact.

Respect the saved live priority order from `overview` before making a heuristic recommendation. Its global `next_unstarted` names the first unstarted identity even when that item lies outside this page; read exact item status for its dependency targets, lifecycle, replacement and preparation facts, and report an existing blocker rather than silently recommending a lower item. Active, review and previously started attempts remain current work, not new starts. Priority does not change dependencies, preparation authority, available actions or independent parallel eligibility.

Read each returned dependency condition as its exact target. A string identity requires the whole prerequisite to be `done` or `superseded`; `{"item":"producer","checkpoint":"usable-api"}` can also be satisfied by a matching committed checkpoint acceptance. Focused status, preview, and generated item, board, and roadmap output retain that distinction and its acceptance status. Overview counts apply the same rule without presenting the full targets. An active producer can therefore have satisfied a consumer's checkpoint dependency while still owing its own remaining work. Acceptance recorded on any retained producer attempt survives later brief changes, rebind, or cancellation; do not infer a blocker merely from the producer's current state. Whole-item dependencies continue to wait for whole-item completion or supersession.

Save only an explicit human priority decision through `pinboard_order`: finish a complete same-revision `pinboard_overview` traversal and put its ordered item identities in `order.expected_order` and the complete authorized permutation in `order.requested_order`, with `order.schema: pinboard-live-order/v1`, exact roots, and trusted `actor_task_id`/`actor_host_id` inside `request`, preserving unmentioned relative order unless the human decided otherwise. A stale rejection needs a fresh complete traversal and reconciliation with the same decision; a committed warning keeps the receipt and names exact CLI view-repair recovery, never order replay. A fresh complete traversal verifies saved order, but after a lost reply it cannot prove this caller committed, because a valid no-op leaves the same order; never blindly replay the mutation.

When the human asks for a new priority recommendation, prefer, in order:

1. evidence preservation or avoidance of an irreversible transition;
2. prerequisites required by the current product objective;
3. runtime, consumer, or user-visible product evidence;
4. foundation work that is concretely cheaper now;
5. optional hardening only after its recorded reopen condition occurs.

Do not turn that ordering into a score. A recommendation remains an explanation, not an automatic product decision.


A dropped item is cancelled work, not successful completion. It is absent from the live queue but retains its definition, attempt and evidence. Exact item status names its `cancel` closure; exact retained-attempt inspection presents `dropped` with no executable continuation, and branch-owner output says `cancelled`. A dropped prerequisite keeps whole-item and unaccepted checkpoint targets unsatisfied; an already recorded matching checkpoint acceptance still satisfies that target. Report the retained repository disposition separately; cancellation proves neither absorption nor integration.

## Initiatives and the roadmap

For an initiative question, use `pinboard_initiative` operation `read` with exact roots and `initiative_id`. For the complete project roadmap, use operation `roadmap` with roots only. This deliberate aggregate read includes complete initiative history, current and terminal members, unassigned live work and relevant external prerequisite context; ordinary quick status and bare `$pinboard` / `/pinboard` orientation use the focused routes above and never call `pinboard_initiative` unless the user asks about initiatives or the roadmap.

The same tool exposes strict `create`, `revise`, `member-add`, `member-remove`, `decision` and `assess` leaves. Discover their exact schema before constructing a change. Writes retain `human`, supplied `date`, `reason`, and actor task/host attribution. Existing-initiative writes compare `expected_revision`; assessments also name the current `evaluation_context`. A goal or success-signal edit creates a fresh unassessed context, while unrelated metadata preserves it. General decisions are separate from goal assessments.

Membership and wave placement grant no lifecycle or execution authority. Delivered means successful item completion; cancelled, superseded and removed memberships earn no delivery credit. Read the page's explicit totals selection and snapshot revision. Every ledger commit regenerates the roadmap, including artifact-only and unrelated changes; complete selected history grows the offline page and per-commit work. Reload the file after regeneration. A committed view warning requires the supported `pinboard views rebuild` repair, never replay of the mutation. Revisit the history/refresh policy only for measured material delays.

# Setup and transitions

Use this section for setup, state contracts, mutations or nested intake. The [main conversation core](#route-common-requests) owns human decisions and replies. Use [the shared runtime adapters](#coding-agent-runtime-adapters) for exact request shapes and the selected runtime instructions inline, for identity and host permissions.

## Start from executable state

Before selecting a deferred Pinboard tool schema, follow the discovery instructions supplied by the initialized connection. If those instructions are absent, read and follow the [native discovery procedure](#packaged-connection-and-first-setup). Load that shared runtime reference when an operation needs its detailed request, startup or recovery contract, including the [current MCP request contract](#current-mcp-request-shapes). It owns exact request-envelope placement; workflow authority and lifecycle decisions remain here.

Use the connected Pinboard MCP surface for item status, item definition and history, brief construction and source preparation, proposal creation, brief publication, overview, saved priority, structural parallel preview, action discovery, attempt inspection, correction context, artifact verification, candidate observation and restoration, preparation and attempt authority, lifecycle transition, human-confirmed close through `pinboard_close`, exact-item cancellation through `pinboard_cancel`, dispatch, review-job, and human-owned PR review, with exact project and work roots on every call. Transitions carry a fresh exact receipt and structured leaf payload; dispatch carries its project receipt and structured environment; review-job carries its exact candidate and caller-selected history identities. Follow the runtime adapter's native callable restoration instructions. Restoration requires the current accepted snapshot context and exact inspected candidate; it neither selects archived history nor creates or launches a checkout. Follow returned effect, retry, and changed-surface accounting.

For requested Pinboard setup, follow the shared policy’s [private adoption rule](#route-common-requests) through loaded skills and the existing private initialization below. `pinboard init` initializes the selected work root; default initialization adds its exact local Git exclusion. It does not install project guidance. Keep project-specific guidance edits and explicit contributor-documentation requests within their separately authorized purpose.

1. For CLI-only operations, invoke `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard`, where `<launcher-root>` is the directory two levels above this skill (`../../scripts/pinboard` relative to it); integration-specific discovery belongs in the runtime adapters, while the launcher-relative executable and CLI contract are common. A prepared Pinboard source checkout uses `<pinboard-source>/.venv`; an installed plugin uses only its marker-backed `<launcher-root>/.pinboard-runtime/environment`. Ordinary launch never invokes uv or consults the managed project's `.venv`, Python dependencies, or uv project. When the launcher returns `pinboard-launcher-result/v1` with `runtime-preparation-required`, run its exact same-launcher `--prepare-runtime` action once with uv available and only the narrow launcher-root write access it names, then retry the original command. That result always reports `pinboard_started: false`, says whether `.pinboard-runtime` changed, and preserves upstream diagnostics; it never proves the requested command ran. Follow its retry requirement for a preparation failure and never construct an ad hoc uv command, cache override, installed-cache locator, or managed-project environment workaround. When the user selected an explicit project root, place `--project-root <root>` before the subcommand on every invocation. Add `--work-root <path>` only when the user separately selected a non-default Pinboard directory; never reuse the project root as the work root or silently fall back to the current directory's default board. For a linked worktree, preserve the shared default ledger and use only its exact resolved absolute `.pinboard` directory in Codex permission recovery; never substitute the checkout-relative path or the whole shared repository.
2. For ordinary project-status orientation, traverse `pinboard_overview` with the exact roots under the [bounded discovery contract](#bounded-discovery). A page is partial until continuation is null; use focused reads for a known item or attempt. A request to read explicitly named context and wait is narrower than project-status orientation and uses only those named reads. When the user has already supplied an exact mutation and its semantic inputs, do not add an overview preflight merely because this skill triggered; use the narrow action query directly.
3. If the exact selected root is unavailable, report `WORKFLOW_UNAVAILABLE`. Initialize `.pinboard` with `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard init --json` only when the user explicitly requests coordinated-work setup. Read only that selected root; do not scan another location or choose a replacement board. An explicit `--work-root` remains at its user-selected location under ordinary root rules. A released predecessor ledger uses the [schema recovery](#authoritative-state) preview and apply sequence at the selected real root while quiescent. When a successful fresh initialization reports optional repository-care skills, relay them once in the user-facing result by presenting `$repository-readiness`, `$slop-cleanup`, and `$maintaining-agent-guidance` as optional next steps. The pointer and Codex setting recommendation are advice only: do not invoke a skill, create work, edit configuration, infer that a repository-care recommendation applies, or infer the effective project setting from them.

4. Require the returned authority to be exactly `sqlite-v11`. If validation fails or another authority is reported, stop state-consuming work and use the recovery procedure in `references/state-and-recovery.md`; never infer a fallback from generated views or archived files.
5. Inspecting SQLite state needs no lease. Prepare one exact leaf payload from the advertised `pinboard_transition` schema. Query the exact action through `pinboard_actions` as project, then call `pinboard_transition` with its complete returned receipt, structured payload, and invoking task and host identity. SQLite checks and commits the complete transition atomically. The negotiated transition leaf schema and action's inline input contract own exact contract diagnosis. Close is not a `pinboard_transition` leaf; apply a discovered close action only through `pinboard_close` as described under [Apply a transition](#apply-a-transition). The retained `close` CLI command is the human's own terminal route, not an agent fallback.
6. Preparation and attempt work use their own renewable leases. For a ready item only, call `pinboard_preparation_authority` with operation `start`, item, task, host, TTL, and exact roots. It selects the current definition and either creates the first claim or transfers an inactive retained claim in one transaction. Renew, release, or revoke preparation authority through that tool. For ready-item recovery and contract diagnosis, use preparation `status` and `start`; for an existing attempt, use attempt `status` and `acquire` when its continuation calls for worker authority. Neither tool exposes a `transfer` leaf. Inspect the named attempt through `pinboard_attempt_inspect` and follow its derived continuation rather than reconstructing ownership from conversation. Acquire worker authority through `pinboard_attempt_authority` with the launched worker's own task and host. A live conflicting holder rejects unchanged; forced revocation requires explicit user authority. Lifecycle state alone does not prove that user input is required; ask only when the recorded condition exposes a product choice the human has not made. If a required precondition is unavailable through a supported read, preserve that missing path as a product defect instead of inventing a value or reading raw SQLite state.

A paused item already has an attempt. Inspect that attempt first, use its current condition and legal actions to explain any human choice, and continue the same attempt. If its accepted scope or Git lineage is stale, publish the matching replacement brief and rebind before selecting its legal resume action. Do not start new preparation for it or diagnose a missing `transfer` operation. At a material choice, say where the work stands, why the person is needed, the practical supported options, what the agent will do after the choice, and what will count as complete; otherwise continue quietly.

When a native invocation, role, authority requirement, artifact shape or retry rule is unclear, use that connected tool's negotiated input and output schema and the exact action's inline input contract. An action's kind, `semantics.effect` and applicable `input_contract.payload_schema` tell its route: a `mutating` action with a payload schema is applied through `pinboard_transition`, except `close`, which is applied only through `pinboard_close`; `dispatch` goes to `pinboard_dispatch`; `inspect` and `continue` are reads or runtime continuation; and `report-blocker` is advisory blocker evidence. Action discovery omits `payload_schema` when no lifecycle payload applies. Separately owned operations, including dispatch, retain their own native request contracts. Never pass an advisory action to `pinboard_transition`. Treat each selected leaf's authority and postcondition independently: acquisition consumes direct identity facts and returns the lease it creates. Do not inspect implementation source or guess fields from neighboring tools. For retained CLI operations only, use `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard tool-contract --json` and one operation selector returned by that static index; follow its exact `cli_usage`, including global roots before the subcommand. CLI discovery includes root resolution, setup, status, validation, view repair, project export, human closure and static code lookup. For an unfamiliar stable code, use `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard code-catalog --json --code CODE`; follow the returned result's exact effect, retry, resource and next step over generic catalog recovery.

For retained CLI commands that support `--json`, treat `pinboard-rejected-operation/v1` as the recovery boundary. `status: rejected` and `state_changed: false` mean this invocation committed no Pinboard effect; correct the input, reacquire authority, or use one returned fresh action exactly as classified. `status: committed-effect` names durable surfaces already changed before the operation stopped; inspect current state and do not replay the mutation. A recovery action with `generation: null` uses direct project authority, while a non-null generation and lease must be copied together. Do not infer success or safety from the prose message when these fields are present.

For native calls, follow the selected tool's strict result schema, effect, retry and changed-surface facts. A `failed-after-publication` or `committed-effect` result names already published surfaces; preserve its exact selectors and inspect current state instead of replaying the call. A committed warning does not undo its receipt. An unchanged rejection may be corrected or refreshed only as its contract permits.

## Ownership

- Let `state.sqlite3` own lifecycle, dependencies, attempts, preparation and attempt leases, proposals, history, and accepted artifact references.
- Let `views/` remain generated human-readable output. Never edit it as authority.
- Let accepted brief and evidence artifacts own execution semantics and review receipts; resolve them through their SQLite artifact references.
- Let proposal fact columns preserve the original intake evidence while disposition columns record the later decision and same-identity items own queue state and position.
- Let public project documentation own stable architecture and domain truth.

Project transitions are direct atomic SQLite changes with task and host audit attribution supplied by the invoking trusted local task. Those strings are not authenticated credentials. Disjoint preparation leases reserve exact ready-item definitions before activation, and disjoint attempt leases authorize active item-local work concurrently. Expiry, release, revocation, and higher fencing generations invalidate retained leased actions.

## Read replacement coverage

Use `pinboard_obligation_coverage` with exact roots inside `request`. For any named pair, select `operation: "pair"` with `source_item` and `replacement_item`; for the current recorded relation, select `operation: "planned-replacement"` with `item_id`. The report lists each obligation of the source's current definition and all replacement obligations whose recorded origin matches its exact item, revision and obligation ID, or marks it uncovered. A valid older origin remains provenance but cannot cover a newer source revision. The latest retained replacement definition remains readable after that replacement finishes. This read records no changes and certifies neither semantic equivalence nor successful completion.

Focused project `close` action detail and cancellation preview include `replacement_coverage` when a current planned replacement exists. Before ending that source, show every uncovered obligation and its practical consequence, and obtain the human's explicit decision about ending it anyway or preserving the work. Recommend preserving unresolved work unless the human has chosen its dismissal. Reuse a prior explicit decision that already covers those exact uncovered facts; coverage creates no extra approval requirement for settled scope. An otherwise-legal explicit ending remains possible. Coverage cannot bypass accepted-attempt review, close legality, or separate cancellation confirmation.

## Apply a transition

Before the first default initialization or when a routine mutation reports `SQLITE_READONLY`, follow the selected runtime’s inline permission recovery. In Codex, apply its protected-project-write rule. Keep one-time Git exclusion authority separate from routine project-data access.

In a complete `revise-item` replacement, `definition.dependencies` accepts whole-item strings and checkpoint targets such as `["whole-item", {"item":"producer","checkpoint":"usable-api"}]`. Each prerequisite item may appear only once, regardless of target form. A checkpoint target must name the stable ID in that prerequisite's current accepted brief; inspect it rather than inventing a checkpoint or using an old brief's ID. A later brief change does not erase committed acceptance evidence for an already recorded dependency. Block payloads still confirm prerequisite item identities from the accepted definition and do not replace its targets.

1. Identify one action as `<kind>:<subject>`. Read its returned `use_case`, `effect`, `permitted_roles`, `subject_kind`, `lifecycle_precondition`, and `practical_result` instead of inferring from the verb. The stable `effect` field says whether the action accepts a lifecycle transition payload; it does not summarize every outer command effect, and dispatch may publish or reuse review evidence while leaving lifecycle unchanged. Treat the exact action record's `authorization` as the runtime authority to forward; the kind-level permitted roles do not replace it. When semantic input is not already settled, use the advertised exact transition leaf schema and prepare its structured payload before selecting the action. `revise-item:<item>` replaces one complete definition after exact revision-and-digest matching; never synthesize a partial patch. `report-blocker:<attempt>` is a worker advisory with no mutation payload; `block:<attempt>` is the project transition for an active attempt; `block-item:<item>` is the project transition for a ready item without an attempt. Blocking may name only dependencies already accepted in the current definition and never changes dependencies itself.
2. For one project change, call `pinboard_actions` with exact roots, role `project`, and structured `action_id` containing the exact kind and subject. Copy its returned action identity and `subject_revision` together as the transition receipt; supply the invoking task and host identity.
3. For an attempt- or preparation-local change, call `pinboard_actions` with exact roots, role `worker` or `preparer`, exact lease and generation, and structured action identity. Copy the returned identity and revision together. Forward the lease and generation unchanged; do not infer authorization from a neighboring role or reconstruct a partial receipt from prose.
4. Call `pinboard_transition` with those exact roots, role, receipt, authority fields, and structured leaf payload. A committed result returns the exact action identity, committed revision, history receipt, effect, changed surfaces, retry disposition, and any generated-view warning. A warning does not undo the authoritative transition. Preserve that receipt and call `pinboard_attempt_inspect` for the derived continuation; never replay a committed transition to obtain it.
5. On `STALE_ACTION`, discard the receipt, reselect only the same exact action, and retry silently while its semantics and payload are unchanged, retained state is safe, and existing authorization can refresh or reacquire the capability. Stop when the action disappears, its semantics, role, or payload changes, authority cannot be refreshed, state is invalid, or the lease or turn deadline cannot fit another attempt, and report only the resulting blocker, changed outcome, unsafe state, or required decision. A freshly selected receipt rejected without an intervening ledger revision is an executable contradiction: preserve the evidence and report it.
6. On `ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE`, do not replay the same command, switch roles, or skip to another lifecycle state. Validate once and refresh only the same exact action under fresh authority. If it disappeared, follow the resulting state and report it only when the user's outcome or next action changed. If it is now available, apply its fresh receipt once under the `STALE_ACTION` rule; treat only an unexplained rejection without an intervening ledger revision as an executable contradiction.
7. If a task is interrupted before a receipt is visible, never replay its retained action. Follow the interrupted-transition recovery in `references/state-and-recovery.md`; authoritative state distinguishes no change from one complete committed transition, and a fresh lease generation fences the abandoned action.
8. Report the practical effect of the returned transition in terms of the human's picture. Run `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard validate` immediately after any non-tool edit to supporting attempt artifacts.

The executable rejects stale definition identities, expired or replaced lease holders, illegal states, invalid dependencies, and inconsistent references. Actions that require current accepted scope remain unavailable to attempts pinned to an older definition; rebind is the explicit active-or-paused recovery that accepts a matching current-definition brief and corrected Git lineage together. It does not decide whether evidence is true, whether work is valuable, or what product behavior should mean.

For an explicit terminal human decision about eligible live work without an accepted attempt, or an absorbed item eligible for superseded closure below, discover the exact project `close` action through `pinboard_actions`, then call `pinboard_close` with ordinary top-level arguments—`project_root`, `work_root`, `receipt` holding only that action's `action_id` and `subject_revision`, `payload` with `outcome`, `reason` and `human_decision`, `actor_task_id` and `actor_host_id`—instead of manufacturing lifecycle states. `human_decision` is the human's explicit close decision in their own words on one line, such as their reply "yes, close it as done, the parser rewrite covers it"; never write it yourself, and when you do not have it, ask the human and stop. Claude Code v2.1.199 or later asks the human to confirm every `pinboard_close` call, and Codex and earlier Claude Code versions may not ask. Antigravity asks through Pinboard's PreToolUse `force_ask` decision, so the close is unavailable in headless `agy -p` runs; when that hook does not run, Antigravity's own approval settings decide. A denied call, including in a non-interactive run, means the human has not confirmed, so report that and seek no other route. `pinboard_transition` refuses a close receipt unchanged. The tool applies one direct atomic project transition and records the decision with the close. Do not add an overview preflight. Use `done` for eligible work without an accepted attempt when the recorded decision or outcome is complete and may satisfy dependents.

An absorbed item with an unresolved current planned replacement to an existing non-dropped item instead closes as `superseded`. First revise every live dependent to target the replacement item or one of its declared checkpoints; otherwise close refuses unchanged with `LIVE_DEPENDENTS`. This route also closes a preserved paused or blocked attempt to `done` and fences its authority while the item ends as `superseded`, without claiming successful completion. Active or review attempts cannot close. Other accepted attempts must resume or rebind and keep their normal evidence-backed review path; a genuine change to accepted semantics requires deliberate item revision, matching brief review, and rebind. Never use `close` to bypass successful-completion review. An intentional abandonment uses the separate cancellation preview/confirmation route; ordinary `close` rejects `dropped`. The returned revision is the durable mutation receipt, so do not create a temporary payload file or replay the transition to prove that it committed. Still perform the fresh exact `pinboard_item_status` operation `item` read required by [workflow-ending replies](#wrap-up-with-facts).

## Cancel after separate exact-item confirmation

This route requires the human to request cancellation of a live item explicitly. A general cleanup or completion request, agent initiative, ambiguous wording and silence supply no authority. Resolve an ambiguous item with one concrete question before previewing. Every Pinboard client sharing the board must use a cancellation-aware build before its first cancellation; if that condition is unknown or cannot be met, stop cancellation and report it. Older builds cannot consume cancellation history, including validation and export. This condition authorizes no installation.

1. Call `pinboard_cancel` with one strict `request`: `operation: "preview"`, the exact `project_root`, `work_root` and `item_id`. Preview is read-only and acquires no authority. Preserve its returned `binding` unchanged.
2. Show the human the exact item ID, title, current state, objective and scope, accepted attempt and branch when present, preparation and worker ownership, and named prerequisites and dependents. Include the returned replacement coverage and resolve uncovered work under [replacement coverage](#read-replacement-coverage). Explain all returned consequences: the item becomes dropped, retained evidence and repository files stay intact, prior Pinboard authority is fenced, and unsatisfied dependent obligations remain unsatisfied. Existing matching checkpoint acceptance evidence remains valid. Cancellation stops no arbitrary local process. Stop or await your own known worker before committing; a worker's future source-file writes are outside the ledger fence.
3. Ask for a **separate explicit confirmation of that exact item after the preview**, recommending cancellation only when it matches the human's stated request. End the turn and wait. An originating request, inferred intent, a general yes to another action, silence or expiry cannot serve as this confirmation. Retain the human's own exact confirmation words; never compose them yourself.
4. After confirmation, call `pinboard_cancel` with `operation: "confirm"`, the same exact roots and `item_id`, the returned `binding`, the human's words as `human_confirmation`, and your trusted current `actor_task_id` and `actor_host_id`. Do not use generic transition, ordinary close or completion as a cancellation substitute.
5. A different resolved board or changed item, definition, attempt, authority, displayed dependency fact or replacement coverage rejects unchanged. Read a fresh preview, show its current consequences and obtain a new separate confirmation; do not silently refresh the binding under old human words. After a committed result, preserve its receipt and read exact item status. A view warning requires its named repair, never replay. Report the commitment as cancelled/dropped, never completed or absorbed, and say whether retained code still needs repository disposition.

The canonical cancellation receipt records the exact displayed preview, binding, human confirmation and actor attribution. These are trusted-local records, not authenticated human authorship or proof of separate chat turns. The outer chat workflow owns the separate human exchange. Cancellation is available even with preparation, an accepted attempt, stale accepted scope or unresolved dependencies; cancellation creates no new prerequisite satisfaction and does not relax reviewed completion.

## Write human-read records

Humans read these records on the board without the transcript, and later agents act on them. This section owns their writing format: pause and `return-for-correction` reasons, `accept-checkpoint` and `accept-review-and-continue` evidence, `revise-item` reasons, and a `continue` checkpoint's `remaining_work`. These fields keep line breaks exactly as written; put them in the JSON string as `\n`. Every other text field stays one line and rejects a line break, including completion evidence, block, reject-proposal and close reasons, the close `human_decision`, defer and reopen conditions, definitions and identities.

1. Open with one plain sentence a human can read alone: what happened or what is needed, in their terms.
2. After a blank line, add only the short labelled lists that carry facts. A return uses `Problem:`, `Fix:`, `Keep:`, `Not authorized:` and `Fails:`. An acceptance uses `Verified:`, `Accepted limits:`, `Next:` and `Not claimed:`. Remaining work is a numbered list in the order the work must happen. A pause or scope-revision reason may need only its lead sentence and one more sentence.
3. Keep identifiers, criterion numbers, checkpoint IDs and quoted requirements exact. Put digests and file references on one final `References:` line.

```text
A fallback capture failure can discard the original cancellation.

Problem:
- `deliverCapturedObservation` drops an exact `CancellationException` from the fallback capture.
Fix:
- Keep the primary and fallback failure facts separately.
- Add a regression through the real controlled source.
Keep: the earlier removal repair and every continuing obligation.
Not authorized: new product decisions or a generic framework.
Fails: brief 43, criterion 2, "Original facts and controls survive the recognizing boundary".

References: review.md sha256 <digest>, finding 1.
```

```text
Two pieces of work remain after this checkpoint; the guidance pass comes last.

1. Rust startup and lifecycle: the awaited lifecycle and the startup warning.
2. A full guidance pass for contradictions, ownership and repetition.
```

The format applies to new records only; never rewrite an existing record. A reply to the human quotes or paraphrases only the lead sentence, never the labelled lists or the `References:` line, and keeps Pinboard mechanics out as [the human's picture](#keep-the-humans-picture-current) requires.

## Nested intake and concern revision

Proposal creation persists immutable facts and a same-identity ready item. It appends at the back by default or uses an explicitly requested one-based position, and relation semantics may add a dependency or proposal origin. It creates no attempt, pauses no current work, and completes nothing. When intake is embedded in ongoing work, keep a compact continuation anchor in the current task context before invoking it:

- the pre-intake objective;
- the next action already promised;
- the exact active or paused item, attempt, proposal, or durable selector that owns the facts after context compaction.

For active delivery or review, also retain the exact source checkout and shared work root, distinct item and attempt IDs, accepted brief identity, protected candidate or selected canonical return history, actual native worker/reviewer handles and their activity, and the worker's lease/generation when held. After a gap, reread the named item, attempt and authority before selecting the next action. An unavailable or rejected read leaves its facts unknown; a corrected invocation uses the same verified subject rather than another board or a guessed latest record.

After persistence and optional notification handling, return to that anchor in the same turn. Re-read the durable selector when compaction made conversational memory uncertain; do not create a scheduler or recovery record. Before the final response, reconcile every announced pending action as completed, durably deferred at an exact owner, or blocked by one exact decision. The anchor is the agent's own state; what the human sees is the [concern receipt](#reconcile-material-concerns-before-reporting-them) and, when something remains open for them, the `Still open:` line.

Conditional follow-up language such as “if this is a production defect, follow it up” authorizes one bounded disposition only after current evidence proves the named condition. If it is false or unproved, make no ledger write; if the exact observation and consequence are already recorded in a live linked owner, reuse that owner. If the condition is proved and the exact concern is new, create at most one `follow-up` or `independent` intake proposal through `$pinboard-intake`, choosing the relation from the evidence, and never turn this authority into a prerequisite, preparation, activation, implementation, notification, or unrelated intake. Record the evidence, relation to current work, and smallest useful next decision, then return to the continuation anchor.

Deliberate steering is distinct from intake and from session or model handoff. Because `ready`, `active`, and `review` states already persist durably on disk across sessions, models, and runtimes, continuing in a fresh session or switching models needs no `pause` transition; reserve `pause` for genuine mid-implementation stops in `active`. Insert a genuine prerequisite only at a safe boundary, pause or block the displaced objective through its legal transition, and name the ordinary `resume:<item>` action that restores it. When the human asks to pause, hold, or sequence an item (for example by adding a bookkeeping dependency or pausing while a reviewed PR waits on another item) in a way that would clear a protected candidate or force a costly `return-for-correction`, `revise-item`, rebind, or re-review ceremony without a genuine scope change, warn the human before mutating state and recommend waiting in place instead. Briefly explain how durable `ready`, `active`, and `review` state works on disk and what to expect when resuming in the same or another session or model (continuation resumes directly from the preserved state and review record without re-review). Recovery is for interrupted or inconsistent state, not the normal route back to preserved work.

When the concern belongs to an existing admitted item and its accepted semantics are incomplete or genuinely changed, read the current definition and discover the project `revise-item` action and call `pinboard_transition` with one complete replacement, exact expected identity, source task, a reason written as a [human-read record](#write-human-read-records), receipt, and roots. A retained attempt then remains pinned and stale; use its legal review-correction path when a candidate is protected, publish a matching revised canonical brief, and rebind the active or paused attempt before continuation. Do not run `return-for-correction` or `revise-item` on a reviewed candidate merely to hold it or record sequencing when accepted scope has not changed unless the human confirms after the rebind and re-review warning above. When no admitted item owns the concern, use `$pinboard-intake` if the user has explicitly authorized preservation.

When an active attempt discovers a prerequisite:

1. preserve its current result and verification;
2. follow the inline [intake procedure](#add-to-the-pinboard) to propose the prerequisite;
3. report the advisory `report-blocker:<attempt>` from the worker context, then have the owning task select the exact project transition: use `block:<attempt>` only when its named dependencies already exist in the current definition, or `pause:<attempt>` when preserving work without such a condition; revise the complete definition first when a newly accepted dependency is required, and never use the intake-only `block-item:<item>` action for active work;
4. implement the accepted prerequisite independently from the current integration base;
5. resume the preserved attempt only after its freshness check passes.

# Work-item consolidation

Use this section only when the human requests combining saved work. The [main conversation core](#route-common-requests) owns decisions and replies. The preview below is read-only until separately approved.

Prepare the complete technical map for the native operation, then explain the proposal in the human's work names: what comes together, what each checkpoint delivers, what waits, and what they need to decide. Keep obligation and origin inventories, placeholder or coverage terminology, action IDs, hashes and payload keys in preparation and application instructions. Include an exact locator in a human reply only when an existing concrete decision or their explicit request needs it.

## Preview work-item consolidation

When a user wants to combine saved work, first ask them to identify the live items to compare if the selection is not already explicit. An optional proposed owner is part of that selection. Keep this first pass read-only: it recommends a smaller backlog but changes no item, relation, priority, proposal, attempt, or accepted artifact. Do not use `merge-proposal` to combine accepted work-item definitions; it only disposes an intake proposal.

1. Read the complete current definition and exact status of each selected item and optional owner for live position, direct dependencies, planned replacements, preparation, and attempts. Use a complete same-revision [bounded discovery traversal](#bounded-discovery) only when the comparison needs the whole live order. Record each item's ID, definition revision and digest, lifecycle state, and sampled project revision in the map; a missing or terminal selection cannot support a current preview. These reads are not one atomic snapshot: reconcile their project revisions, refresh changed selections and affected live relationships, or label the comparison stale and stop short of an assured recommendation. Do not read unrelated retained history or use generated item views as definition authority.
2. Compare the selected objectives, effects, obligations, scope, criteria, exclusions, dependencies, evidence, and stopping or reopening conditions. For each carried obligation, propose its exact recorded `origin`: source `item_id`, `definition_revision` and `obligation_id`. Give every obligation and distinct material scope fact exactly one proposed disposition: owner outcome, named checkpoint, retained independent item, already covered item, or explicit dismissal. Preserve material scope facts with their source revision and location even when they are not definition obligations. Use `pinboard_obligation_coverage` for existing carrying claims instead of inferring them from titles, text equality or export comparisons; an uncovered row remains visible. Keep conflicting claims, uncertain evidence, and unmatched facts visible, and retain a concern independently while its disposition is uncertain.
3. Recommend one owner for one concrete product outcome, or one [campaign](#shape-a-campaign) owner for several outcomes that share a scarce resource or execution window, or that the human prefers to run as fewer, longer stretches. A checkpoint must deliver independent value and leave nonempty work toward the owner's outcome. Keep separate ownership when a consumer needs a result before the owner could deliver it, or when different stopping conditions, uncertainty, or reopening triggers would make one outcome wait on work the human did not choose to bundle. If no coherent owner exists, explain which work needs to stay separate and why, retaining the completed map for application rather than forcing a merge.
4. Build the complete proposed owner definition, then call `pinboard_consolidate` with `request.operation: preview`, exact roots, your current `actor_task_id`, and `selection`. Its `sources` list names each live source and concrete `replacement_cost`; `campaign` names the new or existing `item_id`, `create` boolean and complete current v2/v3 `definition`. Supply the owner's own work and way-of-working obligations there; the operation appends every selected source obligation with a unique ID, unchanged statement and deferral policy, and its direct item/revision/obligation origin. `checkpoint_targets` is empty for whole-campaign waits, or names each outside `consumer`, declared campaign `checkpoint` and `covers_carried_work` explanation for an explicitly proposed earlier wait. The preview selects the current facts together and displays the final campaign, source context, origins, replacements, surviving consumer revisions, queue changes and lifecycle effects. Internal cohort prerequisites become retained binding context; external waits remain in the campaign. Active/review sources and blocking live preparation claims refuse. Active/review owners and consumers can be revised without pausing, fencing or rebinding them, leaving their accepted attempt scope stale.
5. After the read-only native preview, present a short proposal for the human's separate approval. Name the combined outcome and show one row per item being absorbed: its work name, what its checkpoint delivers, what it waits on and any exception. Explain conflicting claims, uncertain evidence and unmatched work where they affect the recommendation. Describe an individual commitment only when its proposed treatment differs from carrying it into the combined work; keep the complete per-obligation and origin map for application. State the pending choices with a recommendation for each. This human view explains the native preview's effects without copying its field inventory; nothing has been applied yet.

## Apply confirmed consolidation

Only after the human separately confirms that exact proposal, call the tool's `confirm` leaf with the same selection, returned `binding`, their exact `human_confirmation`, and your trusted current task/host identities. Confirmation rereads the selected facts under the write lock and atomically applies the whole map, including superseded source endings. Changed relevant facts require a fresh preview and separate confirmation; an unrelated project revision alone does not. Read current coverage afterward. A committed warning keeps its ledger effect: follow its view-repair instruction and do not replay confirmation. This grants no launch, rebind, completion, process or repository authority.

For an existing live replacement whose source work was carried only in prose, use ordinary `revise-item` to attach each exact retained `origin` to its carrying obligation in a complete v3 definition. Keep origin-free obligations explicit with `origin: null`; origin-free definitions use v2. Read `pinboard_obligation_coverage` after revision and reload: only direct origins for the current source revision count. Invalid origins refuse unchanged. Completed replacements remain readable coverage sources, and terminal definitions cannot be revised. Separate close and completion conditions remain unchanged.

A retrospective portfolio comparison can illustrate a recommendation, but label its historical definitions and lifecycle facts as retrospective. Dogfood the procedure separately on an explicit current live cohort and record whether the ledger revision stayed unchanged during that preview; concurrent work may advance the revision, so attribute only observed effects rather than treating equal revisions as the sole proof.

## Shape a campaign

A campaign is one consolidated item that one owner runs autonomously for a long stretch, so the human starts it once and is needed only at grouped sittings and decision batches. Put its complete proposed definition into the native preview before [separate confirmation](#apply-confirmed-consolidation):

- Review the automatically carried source obligations and exact origins. Equal statements from different sources stay separate, because each origin covers only its own source.
- Add the way-of-working obligations with `origin: null`, naming the project's scarce resource and its human steps concretely. They are an intended campaign exception to intake's rule that obligations describe only the product or repository outcome, because the way the campaign runs is what it promises the human:
  1. the first reply after starting or resuming presents the agenda: checkpoint order, offline and live work, every planned human sitting and what each decision unblocks;
  2. the brief declares the named checkpoints in order;
  3. one owner holds the scarce resource and performs only resource-bound steps, while helpers do the rest;
  4. human hands-on steps are batched into as few sittings as possible;
  5. work continues on everything not waiting; when only waiting work remains, the owner pauses with every pending step and decision in one record instead of waiting;
  6. decisions are presented as one batch per pause, each with a recommendation;
  7. reports state results against the accepted outcome, and a case the brief excluded is not reported as unchecked work unless it changes a decision the human must make.
- Record in `evidence` each absorbed item with its definition revision, so its scope, non-scope and acceptance criteria stay binding context, and copy its material exclusions. Record the human's standing instructions there in their own words, such as landing every checkpoint on one branch for one publication, the publication route, cleanup and closing absorbed items; they authorize the outer workflow and are not obligations.

In the opening agenda and later campaign reports, turn these commitments into the human's next useful picture: the accepted outcomes in checkpoint order, what can proceed now, their planned hands-on sittings, and the choices that unblock the rest. Say what each checkpoint achieves and report results against that promise. Keep the full obligation/origin inventory in application instructions; carry waits, exceptions and retained decisions into replies when they affect the human's work or choices. An excluded case belongs in a reply only when it changes a present decision.

Confirmation records replacements and ends absorbed sources as `superseded`, retaining their definitions, evidence and history. Outside consumers wait on the campaign, or on one separately approved declared checkpoint that covers all their carried prerequisite work. A checkpoint can be declared in the item definition before any brief exists; declaration does not enforce execution ordering. Whole-campaign waits remain unsatisfied until the campaign finishes. The human starts or continues the campaign through its ordinary start or attempt route.

# Preparation and dispatch

Use this section when authorized work starts or resumes and before preparing or dispatching it. The [main conversation core](#route-common-requests) owns scope, limitations, opportunity suggestions and the human picture. Use [brief preservation](#cross-boundary-brief-preservation) only for a cross-boundary checkpoint.

Known item and attempt identities use exact item status, definition, attempt inspection and the required authority/evidence reads. Do not preload overview; board-wide discovery follows [bounded discovery](#bounded-discovery) only when the requested decision needs it.

For brief construction, choose the boundary from accepted work and call `pinboard_brief_contract` operation `starter` with exact roots and that boundary. Copy its complete `starter`, choose one returned structural variant at every applicable `selection_path`, replace only those values with complete templates, then fill each semantic `null` from accepted scope and reviewed evidence. Preserve the remaining fields and apply its canonical byte rule, relational constraints and fact-validation boundary. Use operation `full` when the generated schema is needed. Never publish unresolved, partial or invented values. Publication does not verify declared Git facts or prove semantic claims.

Publication verifies the current accepted definition, complete obligation correspondence, and fixed checkout-policy agreement. Activation additionally verifies the brief's owner, branch, base revision, actual checkout classification, and declared source authorities against the exact selected checkout before lifecycle mutation.

When a consumer needs one accepted checkpoint before the producer's whole outcome is complete, record a checkpoint dependency through the inline [intake target syntax](#prepare-one-proposal) or a complete definition revision. Use the stable ID from the producer's current accepted brief and preserve the producer as one item. A whole-item dependency remains appropriate when the consumer must wait for all producer work, including serialization around a scarce resource. Checkpoint satisfaction changes dependency eligibility; preparation, review, and launch authority keep their existing requirements.

For an authorized new concern, follow the inline [intake procedure](#add-to-the-pinboard) through persistence and its immediate-start continuation.

For immediate-start continuation after proposal persistence, start preparation for the same-identity ready item through `pinboard_preparation_authority`. When the accepted checkout policy is isolated, create or select the actual isolated checkout through the runtime adapter before constructing or publishing the brief. Use that checkout as `project_root`, keep the exact shared `work_root`, and read its branch and full base revision there. Do not publish an isolated brief from the original checkout or change the brief to main merely because no worktree exists yet. Publish through `pinboard_brief_publish`, commissioning independent brief review for a cross-boundary checkpoint; activate through the fresh preparer receipt and accepted brief reference. Select project dispatch and call `pinboard_dispatch` to publish the immutable prompt and native envelope. The fresh worker follows the runtime adapter's verifier and startup contract. Submit the candidate through the fresh worker receipt and `pinboard_transition`; inspect its continuation through `pinboard_attempt_inspect` with explicit reconciliation observations or `null`, then follow the one returned operation. Query a fresh action before every transition and copy its receipt as an opaque unit. This sequence does not manufacture scope or bypass the preparation rules below and [review rules](#review-and-repository-disposition).

## Checkout and baseline

Treat an explicit user choice of the main checkout or an isolated worktree as settled. For requested isolation, select the actual isolated checkout—not a feature branch in the original checkout—before recording the brief's branch and base revision, activating, or dispatching; if an existing attempt's recorded Git lineage must change, use the same-attempt replacement-brief and rebind route below first. Discuss integration risk only when observed overlap or conflict makes it concrete or the repository decision requires it.

After selecting a newly created implementation worktree for repository writes, follow the repository's exact worktree-preparation command before Pinboard preparation or implementation source work. Run it once for that checkout; do not substitute global installs or another checkout's mutable dependency directories. If setup fails, follow the runtime adapter's [source-worktree setup recovery](#source-worktree-setup-recovery). When the task changes its own preparation or verification tool, preserve base setup as bootstrap evidence, keep stable installed tooling only for coordination, and verify the changed candidate directly.

Before repository writes or worktree creation, infer the likely integration baseline from project Git evidence rather than assuming `main`, `origin`, or `upstream` are universal: prefer a uniquely resolved remote default branch supported by its symbolic remote head and current tracking or ancestry evidence, refreshing the remote reference when network authority exists and freshness matters, since a local default branch may be stale. Keep strong evidence private when the selected checkout already matches.

Treat weaker evidence as a hypothesis. If the main checkout is on another branch, behind or divergent from the likely baseline, several targets remain plausible, or no strong project clue exists, pause before writes, state the mismatch in one sentence, and ask the smallest confirmation with the best-supported baseline first, for example `Quick reply: 1 use <remote>/<default> · 2 keep <current branch>`. Never silently redefine “main checkout” as whatever branch is checked out.

When an active or paused attempt has a confirmed branch or base mismatch, an older accepted definition, or both, publish a replacement brief for that same attempt that matches the item's current definition and corrected Git lineage. Then use the supported `rebind-attempt:<attempt>` project action with the corrected branch, base revision, and accepted brief reference. Rebinding atomically replaces the attempt's accepted-scope identity and Git lineage, preserves its active or paused state and evidence, fences the previous worker generation, and never changes the checkout. Resume a paused attempt after rebinding. If replacement supersedes an outstanding correction, follow [replacement-brief review recovery](#recover-after-a-brief-replacement) before dispatch. Otherwise, in the corrected environment, select project dispatch, publish or reuse the immutable prompt reference, launch a fresh worker, and require prompt verification before that worker acquires fresh attempt authority and selects leased continuation. The fresh reviewed dispatch checks reviewed authorities against the accepted base commit, so uncommitted authority edits from the attempt do not prevent relaunch. Correction dispatch continues to check the current checkout and requires fresh correction source review when those edits affect reviewed authorities.

Before repository writes begin in the main checkout, establish that it is available: a matching current coding-agent task, exact active attempt, and dispatch checkout establish availability without persistent checkout ownership state, while another writing task there means it is occupied, named by its real title when available.

When the user authorized immediate work without choosing a checkout, select the main checkout without asking when its baseline is strongly resolved, it is available, and isolation has no concrete benefit. Prefer an isolated worktree when independent concurrent work makes isolation useful; otherwise ask the smallest checkout question the baseline or contention evidence supports, with text fallback `Quick reply: 1 main checkout · 2 isolated worktree`.

When the main checkout is occupied, assess overlap only from target-checkout or worktree occupancy, intended write paths, currently changed filenames, and at most the active brief's named owners or source selectors. Separate observations from uncertainty; recommend waiting when files overlap or uncertainty makes waiting safest, otherwise an isolated worktree, and ask one concise question with text fallback `Quick reply: 1 wait for main checkout · 2 isolated worktree`.

Stop after the bounded recommendation unless further evidence is necessary for the user's decision. Do not turn this assessment into a full-diff review, history walk, test run, open-ended investigation, persistent checkout registry, or generic resource-lock subsystem without concrete evidence that the bounded path fails.

## Prepare delegated attempts

For a newly created implementation worktree, complete the repository-owned preparation command described above before acquiring preparation authority or reading implementation sources. Record that successful base setup in the brief's bootstrap when the task changes the preparation command, dependency locks, package-manager contract, launcher, validator, or another tool needed to assess itself. The worker must exercise the changed candidate separately; stable installed tooling remains coordination infrastructure.

Before the owning task publishes either a local or cross-boundary brief, resolve every executable, package, or module named by mandatory verification to a repository-owned entry point, a declared dependency or toolchain, or documented runtime or standard-library support. Resolution is necessary but not sufficient: separately confirm that the exact command is appropriate for this repository's guidance and supported consumers. Apply the shared policy’s [repair responsibility](#keep-assurance-inside-accepted-product-scope) to an in-scope project-owned tool defect or agent-selected unsuitable invocation, correcting it under existing authority while preserving the required evidence. A consumer task diagnoses Pinboard or third-party implementation blockers and recommends resolution through their owner unless that development is explicitly assigned; availability alone grants no implementation scope. If a required capability cannot be resolved or remains degraded, stop its affected preparation without guessing, substituting, repeatedly recovering, or silently omitting the check. Ask the human only for missing authority or a revised scope and evidence contract; runtime permission recovery remains with the runtime adapter.
