When a cross-boundary outcome remains materially broad because it contains multiple independently valuable product effects or distinct required outcomes, regardless of file or command count, make its delivery shape explicit before publication. Record independently useful checkpoints with nonempty required remaining work, or one concrete reason the outcome is indivisible. Measurement, source enumeration, and report-only artifacts are evidence, not independently useful delivery checkpoints. Preserve complete accepted scope across the sequence and keep later required work nonoptional.

When composing any brief for a change that adds an agent-facing output, a failure path, or a multi-step effect, check the managed project's recorded readiness tier or equivalent repository policy. This readiness hook is mandatory only under that existing policy: map the affected capability to a brief contract or criterion sized to it, preserving the exact authority and verification. Use the [agentic-readiness method](#check-the-seven-capabilities) to identify the capability, not to create a new guarantee. Without that policy, keep the hook non-blocking. An explicitly accepted readiness obligation still applies through the general assurance rule above; it does not activate this automatic hook. Guidance written by the current change supplies no retroactive basis, and the hook does not select the optional engineering-health baseline.

Prepare and launch the delegated attempt as follows:

1. After the [material-limitation assessment](#resolve-material-architecture-limitations-before-preparation) is resolved and recorded in the accepted definition, call `pinboard_preparation_authority` with exact roots, operation `start`, item, task, host, and TTL before loading implementation sources or compiling a brief. The ordinary start chooses the current definition and either creates the first claim or transfers an inactive retained claim in the same write transaction; a live conflicting claim or no-longer-ready item is rejected without change, and the item remains ready. Renew the exact lease before it expires throughout authority selection, compilation, publication, correction, and review, and release it if work stops. After expiry, release, or revocation, inspect preparation `status`, call ordinary `start` again with your own task and host, re-read the definition, and revalidate every applicable reviewed-source receipt against the current checkout. Reuse prior preparation only when the returned pin and those receipts remain exact; otherwise discard stale draft or review evidence and rerun the affected selection, publication, and review before activation. A live conflicting holder is never permission to transfer or revoke it.
2. Open one strict `pinboard-work-brief/v4` JSON candidate pinned to the preparation claim's exact definition revision and digest. Resolve the accepted definition's checkout policy to `main` or `isolated`; `coordinator-selected` permits either after the ordinary occupancy decision. Record exactly one correspondence row for every stable accepted implementation obligation, targeting an existing contract, criterion, or permitted deferral without replacement prose. Put `remaining_work` only inside a `continue` checkpoint disposition and write it as a [human-read record](#write-human-read-records); use the fieldless `terminal` disposition only when reviewed completion may close the item. Candidate scope, criteria, verification and any continuing work describe only the product or repository state that the worker must produce for independent review. Never put independent review, integration, publication, disposable checkout or branch cleanup, or terminal Pinboard closure into that worker contract; those are later effects retained by the owning coordinator under the repository-disposition authority. Do not publish until the selected checkout exists, the correspondence is complete, and the checkpoint shape, named source selectors, criteria, and exact checks have completed the applicable preparation below.
3. Give every checkpoint a stable kebab-case ID, separate human title, and one typed `local` or `cross-boundary` variant. Use `local` only when ownership and dependency direction, stored and wire identities, and independently owned consumers remain unchanged, and one production entry point can observe the complete changed path. A README edit plus its referenced image is a representative local family when both remain under the same owner and the edit changes no behavior, dependency, stored or wire identity, or independent consumer. Use `cross-boundary` whenever any condition is false. Local checkpoints retain their lightweight path.
4. Give every checkpoint exactly one tagged architecture-impact value. Use `none` when ownership and dependency direction are unchanged, `read-only` when implementation must conform to a named project-relative authority, and `update-required` when the same candidate must update that authority. Do not defer an architecture update to a separate work item.
5. For a cross-boundary checkpoint, read and follow [the inline brief-preservation procedure](#cross-boundary-brief-preservation) completely: freeze the accepted outcome, assurance model, constraints, stable authorities, and explicit uncertainty, then select the smallest evidence set that can challenge the planned change and compile its exact contracts, coverage, verification, lifecycle disposition, and obligation correspondence. The brief names semantic owners and acceptance boundaries, not every implementation file; start from the machine-readable brief contract rather than a remembered field inventory. Publish the complete structured brief through `pinboard_brief_publish` with exact roots; its accepted `.json` artifact is the sole semantic brief, and its generated Markdown attempt view is read-only convenience output never edited or parsed as authority. Publication checks structural correspondence completeness and forbidden deferrals; independent review owns whether each selected target truthfully discharges its obligation. Commission the required fresh-context review and prepare its digest-bound ready-evidence candidate for dispatch. When the reviewer finds blocking defects, publish its complete `pinboard-work-brief-review-needs-correction/v1` evidence through `pinboard_brief_review` operation `publish` with that exact `brief_artifact_ref_id`; operation `status` on the same reference supplies the verified canonical brief, exact full-brief/checkpoint/ordered-authority digest bindings for independent ready or negative review, latest verified findings, and structured correction targets. Copy its bindings under the public commissioning instructions in brief-preservation; report a missing field or capability under the shared source-scope boundary without consulting installed implementation. Correct and republish before independent reassessment under the reference's bounded-correction policy; a changed canonical digest begins a new negative-evidence stream but does not itself require a fresh reviewer. Needs-correction evidence never authorizes dispatch, changes lifecycle, or acquires authority, and its absence says nothing about ready-review evidence. Resolve incomplete semantics, authority roles, coverage, correspondence, or explicit uncertainty through that bounded correction before implementation, and do not file a code defect for code that does not exist. A local checkpoint skips the cross-boundary procedure but uses the same contract, MCP publication tool, and artifact ownership.
   When several implementation sources need a reusable plan, call `pinboard_brief_source_plan_output` operation `plan-to-file` with the structured manifest, explicit destination, positive batch ceiling and exact roots. The tool writes the same canonical `pinboard-brief-source-plan/v1` bytes that stdout planning would return and emits only a compact receipt; then read every batch in order through read-only `pinboard_brief_sources` operation `emit-file` with that plan path and batch index. On Antigravity, read the plan's selected sources through the Antigravity native-source procedure with native `read_file` instead of `emit-file`. Keep operation `plan` for cases where the complete plan itself is the requested inspection result. Never overwrite a differing destination. Treat a committed selected-output failure as non-replayable and inspect its exact path before choosing a new explicit destination.
   When the accepted item or brief explicitly selects the optional engineering-health baseline, also read [the inline engineering-health baseline](#optional-engineering-health-baseline) and preserve its representative contract proof in the brief's authorized contracts and verification. Do not load it because work merely appears complex or cross-boundary, and do not turn it into a default requirement.
6. Call `pinboard_actions` for exact `activate:<item>` as preparer with its lease and generation, then `pinboard_transition` with that receipt, the same authority, and only `brief_artifact_ref_id` in the payload. The shared boundary reads the accepted brief, requires its owner to match the preparer, and verifies the exact current definition, checkout classification, branch, HEAD, and reviewed authorities; the primary checkout is `main` regardless of its current branch, and only a registered linked worktree of the same common repository is `isolated`. The locked transaction rechecks the live definition pin, consumes the preparation claim, and creates the attempt; rebind and replacement-brief resume repeat the definition and checkout check. Announce the brief link after activation or resume. Once active, select exact project-only `dispatch:<attempt>` without worker authority and build the structured `pinboard-dispatch/v2` environment: runtime, background disposition, checkout, branch, starting revision, host, required fresh context, bounded lease TTL, and already-authorized permissions. Dispatch rechecks the current definition and actual checkout classification; Pinboard validates these declarations but neither grants nor enforces runtime access.
7. Call `pinboard_dispatch` with exact roots and `dispatch.kind: ordinary` for a local launch, or `reviewed` with the independent `brief_review` object and a caller-chosen `review_id` label for initial cross-boundary work, carrying the fresh project `receipt`, stable `checkpoint_id`, structured `environment`, and explicit `prompt: null`. After return-for-correction, use `kind: local-correction` for a local checkpoint with an independent review bound to the accepted brief, or `kind: correction` for a cross-boundary checkpoint with a fresh effective contract review; both require the exact selected `correction_history_id`, returned candidate, and canonical reason, and cross-boundary correction refreshes source receipts from the implementation checkout. Dispatch rechecks selected bytes before publication and returns immutable prompt identity, publication accounting, and one exact runtime-specific native launch recipe; it creates no task or worker authority. Call exactly `native_launch.tool` with exactly `native_launch.arguments`: never add, remove, shorten, reformat, or reconstruct an argument from `prompt_reference` or prompt bytes, and never copy the prompt body into the launch call. A supplied `prompt` only checks exact canonical bytes. A worker launched from different arguments is invalid: stop it and use a fresh context with the returned recipe instead of coaching or resuming it. Never dispatch a ready item or require authority before the worker exists.
8. The worker follows the runtime adapter's prompt-verification and startup contract: verify and read the exact named prompt, use its complete canonical brief and bootstrap, obtain its own trusted post-launch runtime identity, use the verified host, acquire own authority, and select the leased continuation. Retain that identity and returned lease and generation. Successful delivery continues through current result evidence, candidate observation, own-leased submission, protected-review confirmation and lease release; do not coach a worker that returns after only editing source. Never substitute a parent/session identity, invent a pre-launch worker identity, or edit its changing checkout or review candidate.
9. Wait until the worker finishes or needs attention. A wait timeout, progress update, or successful launch is not a terminal result.
10. After completion, read `result.md` or `blocker.md`, inspect the stable candidate, and announce the new or materially refreshed result or blocker under the readable-artifact rule. Call `pinboard_attempt_inspect` with exact roots, attempt, and either `reconciliation: null` or fresh outer-owned reconciliation observations, then follow its one continuation. An incomplete worker return or blocker does not transfer implementation, submission, or review ownership to the coordinator; preserve it and follow the returned continuation or fix the supported product blocker before a fresh launch. When inspection names review, render the exact candidate-bound `review-job` and commission its returned native envelope as a fresh-context subagent from this outcome-owning task. A rejected review job publishes no reviewer prompt: correct its stated precondition, and never construct a substitute prompt or direct the reviewer toward approval. After a favorable verdict, record its exact candidate-bound ready identity before resumed inspection can select repository work. Then process the complete returned verdict through the [current-responsibility review route](#coordinate-review-responsibility-and-checkout-use).

The canonical dispatch prompt identifies the brief, checkpoint, declared environment, trusted worker identity source, and result or blocker paths. It includes the exact accepted brief bytes rather than a restatement, so every acceptance semantic, check and deferral reaches the worker without an indirect instruction fetch. The transport-owned envelope adds the exact verifier, acquisition, continuation and successful-return instructions. Change the attempt first when its contract is wrong.

Do not end the owning turn merely because implementation started. End with a running worker only when the user explicitly requested background execution; report that review by a separate reviewer in the current coding agent remains pending and perform it before any acceptance transition.

## Recover a worker or reviewer launch response

A lost successful response or a rejected native launch does not erase the accepted prompt. Recover through a fresh validated tool request when current facts still permit it:

1. Inspect the exact item, attempt, worker authority and actual native task activity. Establish whether publication committed and whether a valid worker or reviewer is already running. Continue a valid worker through its actual handle; stop an invalidly launched context. Do not launch a competing writer or resume a reviewer launched from altered arguments. Missing activity or stop capability leaves that launch pending.
2. For worker dispatch, read the current correction context when applicable and discover a fresh project dispatch action. Preserve the selected current return, accepted brief, exact source checkout, candidate and authorized environment. If the original correction assessment was lost, recover its exact accepted bytes from a retained verified artifact reference or `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard --project-root <checkout> --work-root <work-root> export --json`, saving the export privately. The export includes accepted references and contents; select the unique assessment bound to the current brief, returned snapshot and canonical reason, verify its size/digest and accepted reference through `pinboard_artifact_verify`, and decode that existing assessment. Export materializes the whole project and can fail on unrelated retained corruption. Missing, ambiguous, unavailable or stale bytes stop this recovery; do not write a replacement assessment for the same publication subject.
3. Request `pinboard_dispatch` again with the fresh receipt and exact valid evidence, or `pinboard_review_job` again for the exact submitted candidate and selected histories. Both revalidate current bindings and reuse byte-identical accepted artifacts. A differing correction assessment remains a collision; stale bindings reject. `do-not-retry` forbids blind replay of a committed invocation, not a new request after these observations. Never replay a lifecycle transition to recover a launch response.
4. Launch only the newly returned `native_launch.tool` and `native_launch.arguments`. Codex receives a fresh task name on each response, so a pre-verification task-name collision is resolved by a fresh response rather than editing the old name or digest. Verify the new prompt reference and follow its startup contract. Keep worker submission and separate candidate review in the delivery sequence.

This recovery creates no new launch storage and proves no native task ran. Stop on a current pause, conflicting worker, unresolved scope or effect decision, changed binding, or missing required capability. Preserve repository-mandated executors and runtime permissions; an alternate client or command requires its own explicit authority.

# Cross-boundary brief preservation

Use [the shared runtime adapters](#coding-agent-runtime-adapters) and the selected runtime instructions inline, for fresh reviewer launch and waiting. The preparation and review contract below is shared across integrations.

Use this procedure only for a typed `cross-boundary` checkpoint. It projects named architecture, plans, and accepted evidence into a reviewable execution contract before implementation. A checkpoint is `local` only when ownership and dependency direction, stored and wire identities, and independently owned consumers remain unchanged, and one production entry point can observe the complete changed path. A README edit and its referenced image may stay local when they retain one owner and change none of those facts or product behavior. If any condition is false, use `cross-boundary`. A local checkpoint does not add contracts, reviewed-authority coverage, lifecycle declarations, or an independent brief review.

For broad autonomous work, require the Pinboard workflow's short human-facing scope confirmation before preparation begins. Compile the canonical brief to preserve that stated outcome, principal read and touch surfaces, approximate magnitude, and surprising exclusions; never use the private brief to introduce a consequential narrowing or widening that the human did not see. The confirmation is declarative and does not repeat an authorization question already answered.

## Freeze semantics and select stable authorities

Before writing contracts or coverage rows, freeze the accepted outcome, assurance model, constraints, non-goals, provenance, compatibility, current architecture decisions, and explicit uncertainties. Apply the shared policy’s [assurance boundary](#keep-assurance-inside-accepted-product-scope): distinguish in-scope defects and accepted assurance obligations from material new obligations and speculative risks. Derive stable semantic authorities from those facts rather than guessing the implementation diff. Select the decision, policy, architecture, or external-contract owners needed to challenge the proposed behavior and verification. The brief must make likely owners and uncertainty discoverable; it does not need to predict every file implementation will touch.

Keep the preparation read proportional to the proposed result. For a routine cross-boundary documentation or guidance change, select the smallest authoritative sections and real consumer or generated projection that can disprove the planned story. Do not require unrelated production owners, complete repository traversal, or a fixed-point file inventory. Tests may prove a contract but do not replace its semantic owner. `pinboard_brief_sources` proves the bytes selected by a manifest; it does not prove semantic completeness.

Widen during preparation only when the accepted change itself crosses architecture, persistence, wire, lifecycle, compatibility, trust, or a dynamic-consumer boundary, when the material-limitation method requires its foundation, or when explicit uncertainty prevents a truthful contract. At such a boundary, include the relevant decision or effect owner, direct caller or consumer, independently required conversion, and cheapest real evidence that can falsify agreement. Do not turn that focused trace into a repository-wide pass unless the accepted scope explicitly selects one.

Challenge the selected authorities before canonical publication. Commission one bounded read-only reviewer as a subagent using the accepted definition, architecture declaration, draft contracts, explicit uncertainty, source manifest, and the minimum search or inspection needed to test their roles. Its results return automatically to the owning task; do not create or message another task for this subordinate review. The reviewer identifies missing stable authorities, unsupported roles, unresolved uncertainty, and any concrete widening trigger. Resolve those findings before compiling the brief. This draft check does not replace the required independent review of the canonical checkpoint.

Represent and measure the selected authority set as a structured strict `pinboard-brief-sources/v1` JSON manifest with one row per exact selector:

```json
{
  "schema": "pinboard-brief-sources/v1",
  "sources": [
    {
      "authority_id": "architecture",
      "selector": "ARCHITECTURE.md#Dependency direction",
      "families": ["ownership", "dependencies"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Use one selector with several families instead of repeating or nesting the same selection. For read-only review, call `pinboard_brief_sources` operation `plan` with exact roots, the structured manifest, and positive `max_batch_bytes`, then call its `emit` leaf for each batch in ascending order. The plan and every batch must fit the presented-result limit. If the plan reports its actual size above that limit, split the manifest into smaller source selections and plan and read each selection without publishing a plan or asking the human to replan. Preserve source order and the selected digest for each selection. If a batch rejects because one line cannot fit, narrow the selector or fix the source line before continuing; do not treat truncated output as reviewed text.

When an explicit durable plan is needed, call the write-capable `pinboard_brief_source_plan_output` operation `plan-to-file` with one destination, require its compact receipt, then use read-only `pinboard_brief_sources` operation `emit-file` with that saved plan path and each batch index. Plan publication writes only the selected destination and remains a write operation.

On Antigravity, a coordinator or brief reviewer still plans through `plan` or `plan-to-file` for the selected digests and line spans, but reads every selected source through the Antigravity native-source procedure with native `read_file` instead of `emit` or `emit-file`. That read is not verified against the plan digest; dispatch's reviewed-authority digest check still rejects a selected source that changed after planning.

Preserve each selector and selected digest as its read receipt. Across corrections, reuse exact unchanged receipts and reread only changed owners plus neighboring records whose meaning depends on them. If output truncates, continue from the first unread boundary without replaying returned content.

If the selected set plus working headroom cannot fit, narrow selectors, split only a semantically independent checkpoint, or move mechanical comparison into validated tooling. Do not omit an accepted requirement, prohibition, explicit uncertainty, lifecycle sibling, or consumer merely to fit context.

## Compile canonical JSON

Choose the accepted local or cross-boundary scope, then call `pinboard_brief_contract` operation `starter` with exact roots and that boundary and prepare a strict `pinboard-work-brief/v4` JSON candidate by copying its complete `starter` object. For every applicable path in `structural_choices`, choose exactly one returned variant and replace the starter value at that path with its complete template. The initial tagged value is only the first valid template, not a fixed semantic choice. Then replace every semantic or identity `null` only with accepted scope, reviewed authorities, observed consumers, and explicit verification; preserve all other fields, and do not omit keys or hand-author a partial approximation. Read the selected checkout's actual branch and full Git revision immediately before filling `branch` and `base_revision`; never invent or abbreviate them. The structural choices, canonical byte rules, relational constraints, and fact-validation boundary are construction aids, not semantic evidence. Use operation `full` when the complete generated brief schema is needed; the negotiated publication schema supplies exact native publication facts. Pinboard decodes the completed candidate directly into frozen records with unknown fields forbidden, validates its cross-references, canonicalizes it with sorted object keys and one final LF, and publishes the immutable accepted `.json` artifact through `pinboard_brief_publish` with exact roots and the complete structured candidate. Publication does not resolve branch or base revision against Git and does not prove semantic claims. This JSON artifact is the sole semantic brief. The generated Markdown attempt view is read-only output and must not be edited or parsed as input.

The root record contains:

- schema and artifact identity: `schema`, positive `artifact_revision`, `attempt_id`, `item_id`, `branch`, `base_revision`, and `owner_task_id`;
- accepted scope: positive `revision` and lowercase SHA-256 `digest`;
- human context: `title`, `outcome`, `supported_production_roots`, `product_decision_and_provenance`, `testing_strategy`, `scope`, `bootstrap`, `compatibility`, and `non_goals`;
- one tagged `checkpoint` record.

Use the existing human-context and checkpoint fields to preserve the material-limitation assessment; do not add a consent field or side-channel receipt. When no relevant unacknowledged material limitation is crossed, state that evidence-backed result in `product_decision_and_provenance`. When a limitation is accepted, that field records the exact decision and ordinary explicit human acknowledgement, while scope and non-goals bound its effect. The checkpoint must be `cross-boundary`, its architecture impact must be `update-required` for the current-truth owner, and its contracts, reviewed authorities, coverage, criteria, and verification must account for every affected owner and consumer plus the observable reopening condition. Generic authorization for the surrounding task is not equivalent provenance.

Use those same existing fields to preserve the supported assurance model. A mandatory verification or blocking guarantee must trace to accepted scope or an exact contract or criterion, applicable repository policy, an exact reviewed product-authority family, a named production consumer, or an observed supported-path failure. Broad correctness prose, an exploratory failing test, public narrative, and newly written skill prose are not product authority for another guarantee. If a proposed material expansion lacks support, resolve the shared policy’s concrete human decision before placing it in scope, contracts, criteria, or verification. Do not add a schema field unless a paired or otherwise accepted behavioral run demonstrates that these existing fields cannot preserve the distinction; first name the exact schema, codec, projection, tool-contract, review-job, compatibility, and architecture widening required.

For each mandatory verification entry, resolve every named executable, package, or module to a repository-owned entry point, a declared dependency or toolchain, or documented runtime or standard-library support. Treat that resolution and semantic appropriateness as separate checks: repository evidence must also show that the exact command fits the supported entry points and consumers rather than merely being available to execute.

Challenge any proposed local fix against its foundation. If it preserves, masks, or deepens an unacknowledged material limitation, resolve that architecture checkpoint before preparation rather than treating the compensating layer as a complete bounded fix. A defect against accepted behavior remains a defect, and a speculative risk without evidence on a supported path does not become mandatory scope.

Use one built-in design lens while compiling the brief: prefer existing canonical typed values and direct composition. Introduce a helper, wrapper, protocol, projection, or conversion only when it owns a current semantic boundary, meaningful complexity, reuse, or genuine substitution. Do not recreate an existing concept as a parallel tuple, dictionary, or field-by-field mirror. Genuine substitution includes a narrow required dependency used by the production path even when only tests provide an alternative. This lens shapes the proposed implementation; make it a mandatory contract or verification only when accepted scope or reviewed repository policy authorizes it.

For test access, apply [the test-seam distinction](#choose-explicit-test-seams). Surface a proposed material test workaround or actual scope/instruction conflict in the existing testing strategy and constraints rather than treating hidden access or manufactured preconditions as a clean substitute. Ordinary permitted seams need no label or separate approval.

When a cross-boundary checkpoint extends behavior governed by interacting conditions or operations, read and apply [Preserve independent decision gates](#preserve-independent-decision-gates). Project its condition inventory, sibling trace, mixed counterexample, and focused test or equivalent evidence into the checkpoint's existing contracts, criteria, coverage, and evidence. Do not load the method for an ordinary change with no conditional interaction.

When a checkpoint introduces or changes a command or closed-variant family across several production owners, or places dynamic dispatch on that path, read and apply [developer-navigation.md](#trace-developer-navigation). Project its representative trace, sibling simulation, justified exhaustive sites, and explicit dynamic-wiring failure mode into the checkpoint's existing contracts, criteria, coverage, and evidence. This is a bounded prevention lens for the changed family, not authority for a repository-wide readiness assessment.

Every checkpoint has a stable kebab-case `checkpoint_id`, separate human `title`, `outcome_description`, architecture impact, nonempty acceptance criteria, nonempty mandatory verification, and explicit deferrals. Its `boundary` tag selects one closed shape:

- `local` contains the common fields only;
- `cross-boundary` additionally requires `outcome: independently-buildable`, nonempty contracts, reviewed authorities, authoritative coverage, and one lifecycle partition.

Every current checkpoint also selects exactly one tagged `disposition`. Use `continue` with the sole `remaining_work` field, written as a [human-read record](#write-human-read-records), when acceptance pauses the attempt for named same-item work. Use fieldless `terminal` only when the checkpoint may close the item after protected-candidate review. Never infer this choice from checkpoint history, boundary kind, prose, action labels, or caller intent. Current operations require strict v4. Exact original v2/v3 briefs are historical facts for supported archive, package and completion consumers only; they provide no current execution, status or recovery route. Original v3 package reviews bind the full original canonical brief digest, including root `remaining_work`, independently of archive membership.

When a checkpoint owns structural cleanup, its typed scope and acceptance criteria must name the readable typed consolidation, the direct orphan families to recurse through, and the evidence from one fresh fixed-point pass. Reference the repository's recursive-cleanup procedure for the method instead of duplicating it here; the generated Markdown projection remains non-authoritative.

When that cleanup collapses a closed classification, the contract must identify every duplicated encoding, equivalent alternative-handling branch, proposed canonical owner, and independently required boundary shape. It must distinguish label-only vocabularies, data-bearing alternatives, and context-dependent decisions; require equivalent branches to share one handler without erasing alternatives that another consumer distinguishes; and require exhaustive conversion at retained wire, storage, or presentation boundaries. Apply the developer-navigation reference at the complete depth explicitly selected by the accepted cleanup contract in addition to the bounded prevention lens above. Acceptance evidence must report core decision points, justified exhaustive sites, explicit boundary conversion, representative sibling edit sites, dependency volume, and source-size change separately, then name the fixed-point pass and the product distinctions deliberately retained. Reject a brief that prescribes one representation category for every closed family, treats exhaustiveness as a layer-by-layer quota, rejects dynamic dispatch without considering its ownership, or treats smaller source or dependency counts as proof of a simpler decision model.

Architecture impact is tagged by `kind`:

- `none` records a reason ownership and dependency direction are unchanged;
- `read-only` records one project-relative authority selector and conformance reason;
- `update-required` records the authority selector that must change in the same candidate and why.

Each contract records `invariant`, `authority`, `consumer`, `failure`, `verification`, `revalidation`, and a tagged `authorization_basis`. Each mandatory verification record has an `obligation` and the same authorization basis. Use exactly one basis:

- `accepted-scope` with the current `item_id` and positive `scope_revision`;
- `authority`, `repository-policy`, or `existing-consumer` with an exact reviewed `authority_id` and `family`.

Dispatch checks basis reference integrity against the current SQLite attempt. The independent reviewer owns semantic truth: reject a syntactically valid source used under the wrong role, such as code cited as repository policy, a validator cited as a production consumer, or newly written prose cited as product authority. Verify that every mandatory tool, threshold, platform, compatibility obligation, and hardening check is required by accepted scope or selected authority bytes. Keep proportionate exploratory checks outside the mandatory list.

Each reviewed authority records a unique kebab-case `authority_id`, exact `selector`, selected-byte `reviewed_sha256`, and one or more unique kebab-case `families`. A selector is a project-relative file, optionally followed by `#` and one literal unique Markdown H1–H6 heading. Whole-file digests use unchanged bytes. Heading digests use the heading through the line before the next heading of equal or higher level, with LF line endings and one final LF.

Give every reviewed authority family exactly one coverage record. It names `authority_id`, `family`, `distinction`, `consumer`, `counterexample`, and one tagged `owner` disposition:

- `contract` with an exact contract invariant;
- `acceptance` with an exact criterion number;
- `deferred` with an exact deferral ID;
- `not-applicable` with a concrete reason.

Never defer or mark not applicable an in-scope prohibition. Missing coverage is a brief defect, not implementation discretion.

Lifecycle partition is tagged by `kind`. Use `not-applicable` with a reason when the checkpoint changes no related lifecycle operations. Use `required` with one record per related operation when adjacent operations consume related states. Each record names `operation`, `source_state`, `authority`, `evidence`, `effects`, and one cheapest `illegal_sibling`.

## Review the compiled contract

Commission one read-only reviewer as a fresh-context subagent after compiling the checkpoint and before implementation. Its results return automatically to the owning task; do not create or message another task for this subordinate review. The reviewer task identity must differ from the attempt owner and every draft authority reviewer. Give the reviewer the canonical checkpoint, the same source plan, the exact accepted brief reference and roots, and the [public-contract and source-scope boundary](#public-contracts-and-source-scope). Have it read `pinboard_brief_review` with `request: {operation: status, project_root: <exact checkout>, work_root: <exact work root>, brief_artifact_ref_id: <accepted reference>}` and copy the returned binding fields. If that read or a required field is unavailable, it reports the exact missing input and affected review subject before dependent effects; it does not consult installed implementation or invent readiness. It must:

- confirm that the selected authorities preserve the accepted outcome, constraints, stable decisions, and explicit uncertainty; when a concrete widening trigger exposes another semantic owner, return one bounded correction package and stop before row-by-row review;
- inspect every selected source exactly once and classify its claimed semantic role;
- verify every contract, criterion, mandatory verification basis, architecture declaration, and semantic source role;
- resolve every executable, package, or module named by mandatory verification to repository evidence, then separately reject commands that are mechanically available but inappropriate for the repository's supported entry points and consumers;
- reject a mandatory or blocking assurance obligation that lacks an accepted basis, and reject both unsupported expansion and a proportionality-based waiver of accepted hardening;
- trace every reviewed family to exactly one coverage owner;
- test each cheapest counterexample and every lifecycle sibling;
- reject unsupported, absent, ambiguous, or contradictory coverage rather than asking the implementer to infer it.
- verify that every material limitation named or exposed by the checkpoint has exact accepted acknowledgement and a coherent current-architecture update, and reject generic task authority, an unacknowledged foundational limitation hidden by a compensating layer, or a local checkpoint that introduces such a limitation.

When blocking findings remain, publish their complete structured `pinboard-work-brief-review-needs-correction/v1` record through `pinboard_brief_review` operation `publish` with exact roots and `brief_artifact_ref_id`. Its identities bind the full canonical accepted brief, checkpoint, ordered authority set and independent reviewer. Recover the exact canonical brief and verified latest findings through operation `status` for that reference; no lease is needed; inline publication needs no file, while the declared `publish-file` input accepts the same complete review from an exact verified file. Follow the returned status request and corrected-brief publication target using the [current MCP shapes](#current-mcp-request-shapes). A needs-correction record is not ready dispatch evidence, and no negative evidence means only that this exact subject has no accepted negative record. Neither result grants readiness, lifecycle change or authority.

Correct the JSON candidate when coverage is incomplete, increment its artifact revision, and republish the complete structured brief through `pinboard_brief_publish` before producing new digest-bound review evidence against the corrected accepted artifact. A changed canonical brief digest begins a new negative-evidence stream. Use the same independent reviewer to verify bounded corrections by default; changed artifact bytes alone do not justify another fresh full review. Reuse unchanged source receipts, reread changed owners, and inspect only neighboring records whose meaning depends on the correction. When a correction exposes an ordinary caller, projection, or generator, add its owner and relevant siblings as one bounded relationship set rather than one file per round. Commission another fresh reviewer when the correction changes accepted scope, architecture direction, lifecycle semantics, persistence or migration behavior, or whenever concrete evidence identifies a material blind spot that the prior reviewer cannot independently challenge.

For an oversized completed brief or independent review, use the corresponding verified record file input instead of retransmitting the record inline. Hash the raw selected JSON; accepted artifact bytes and all independent readiness, binding, freshness and collision checks remain canonical and unchanged. This declared input does not provide a missing-tool fallback.

## Prepare and publish review evidence

Initial reviewers copy `accepted_brief_sha256`, `checkpoint_sha256` and `reviewed_authority_set_sha256` from either successful `pinboard_brief_review` status variant for the exact accepted artifact. The read verifies accepted bytes before deriving these values; `accepted_brief.sha256` is the same full-brief binding. Obtain attempt/checkpoint identities and coverage owners from its returned `brief`, supply your own trusted independent reviewer identity, and assess coverage or findings independently. Missing bindings follow the shared [public-contract recovery](#public-contracts-and-source-scope). A local checkpoint does not use this review route.

Canonical encoding uses the application JSON codec with sorted object keys. The brief artifact adds one final LF. Digest inputs do not add presentation bytes:

- `checkpoint_sha256` is SHA-256 of the canonical encoded checkpoint record;
- `reviewed_authority_set_sha256` is SHA-256 of the canonical encoded ordered tuple of reviewed-authority records;
- each `reviewed_sha256` remains the digest of the selected source bytes.

For initial dispatch, prepare strict `pinboard-work-brief-review/v3` JSON with `attempt_id`, stable `checkpoint_id`, `accepted_brief_sha256`, `checkpoint_sha256`, `reviewed_authority_set_sha256`, independent `reviewer_task_id`, `status: complete`, `verdict: ready`, and one coverage result per brief coverage record. `accepted_brief_sha256` is SHA-256 of the complete canonical accepted brief bytes, so checkout selection and obligation correspondence are part of the reviewed identity. Each result repeats the exact `authority_id`, `family`, and tagged owner, records `verdict: covered`, and states the concrete `counterexample_result`. The strict original ready-review v2 reader serves historical checkpoint-package bindings to original brief v2 only. Its exact facts cannot authorize current dispatch, checkpoint acceptance or recovery.

For all three correction review forms below, `assessment` is a nonempty JSON string containing the independent reviewer's prose assessment of the complete accepted starting candidate and proposed correction.

For a returned candidate, read `pinboard_correction_context` before implementation changes the checkout. Its `reuse_eligible` and `reuse_blockers` report whether the accepted brief, every reviewed source, and the exact accepted ready review still support coverage reuse. The read is advisory; dispatch checks those facts again. When reuse is eligible, prepare strict `pinboard-correction-source-review/v2` JSON with the exact `accepted_brief_sha256`, an independent `reviewer_task_id`, the accepted `starting_candidate`, the canonical `correction_input`, and a fresh `assessment` of that candidate and reason. The v2 record reuses only unchanged ready coverage, never the earlier candidate assessment.

When reuse is blocked, prepare strict `pinboard-correction-source-review/v1` JSON with a complete new contract review. Its required fields are:

- `contract_review`: the complete current v3 review, including `accepted_brief_sha256`, bound to the effective brief after recomputing only selected authority digests;
- `starting_candidate`: the caller-selected accepted portable candidate snapshot identity, with `role: candidate`, `kind: evidence`, `key`, `revision`, `selector`, `content_sha256`, and `size_bytes`;
- `correction_input`: the exact canonical `return-for-correction/v1` reason input;
- `assessment`: the independent reviewer's concrete assessment of that complete starting candidate and proposed correction.

The local counterpart, `pinboard-local-correction-source-review/v1`, uses the same fields as the v2 correction review above, bound to the exact accepted local brief and an independent reviewer.

When replacement of the accepted brief supersedes an outstanding correction, first follow the coordination skill's [replacement-brief review recovery](#coordinate-review-responsibility-and-checkout-use). Historical return selection for review is not current correction-dispatch authority.

Correction-context and both return-context selections provide compact evidence instead of inline snapshot bytes. Call `pinboard_artifact_verify` with the exact returned `starting_candidate_verification` arguments, then read only the accepted file named by `starting_candidate_reference.selector` under the exact work root. Verify its complete raw bytes against the returned SHA-256 and byte size before decoding. Require the decoded snapshot's identity, provenance, diff digest/size and exclusions to agree with `starting_candidate` and `starting_snapshot_metadata`, then decode and inspect the complete original diff through bounded output. Do not emit the full encoded snapshot or treat metadata, successful byte verification, or coverage-reuse eligibility as candidate review. If verification, decoding or complete inspection fails, stop without an assessment.

For exact-return correction, compare the checkout with the snapshot. A commit requires the exact clean HEAD and accepted-base binary diff; a working-tree candidate requires the exact branch, HEAD preimage and binary diff. The current reader permits only compatible object-ID abbreviation differences in Git index headers, as described in [Immutable artifacts](../../../ARCHITECTURE.md#immutable-artifacts); retain the original accepted bytes, hashes and candidate identity for every evidence binding. Test-only changes belong to this complete candidate even when selected authority digests do not change. Both correction leaves require the exact current correction history identity; retained ready-review v2 evidence cannot authorize either. Current initial v3 review and historical checkpoint proof remain unchanged.

Call `pinboard_dispatch` with exact roots and its `reviewed` leaf carrying the structured independent `brief_review` and exact `review_id`. A returned cross-boundary candidate uses `reuse-correction` with the v2 record when context reports eligibility, or `correction` with the v1 full review when a blocker is present. Report the named blocker and supported full-review action once; do not repeat unchanged status. Copy the fresh project receipt, checkpoint ID, selected `correction_history_id`, and structured environment, and supply `prompt: null`. Dispatch validates and canonicalizes evidence before application-owned publication, creates it once, reuses byte-identical evidence and preserves differing collisions as rejected evidence. Choose `review_id` yourself: Pinboard never issues one and no context read returns it. It is one path component, such as `correction-review-1`, that only names the preserved rejected evidence after a collision. Reuse the same label when retrying identical evidence; differing evidence returns a do-not-retry review collision, so assess it before choosing a new label for a distinct submission. An ordinary initial leaf may reuse exact already accepted ready evidence. Review publication remains cross-boundary-only and never changes the canonical prompt.

Dispatch reselects the current action and accepted brief, verifies the stable checkpoint ID, canonical checkpoint and ordered-authority digests, selected-source digests, reviewer independence, exact coverage, and immutable evidence before returning the launch prompt. Correction publication additionally binds the complete semantic candidate state and exact correction reason, and rechecks the checkout before returning launch. Receipt IDs, reviewer identities and recording timestamps do not create new subjects. Byte-identical evidence is reusable; differing evidence about an actually identical subject retains the existing collision contract.

## Reuse during implementation review

Inspect the candidate's actual test access under [the test-seam distinction](#choose-explicit-test-seams), including coupling omitted by textual-reference counts. Challenge material contortions that evade a constraint or manufacture preconditions; preserve narrow ordinary dependency seams and supported dynamic protocols. Tie blocking feedback to the accepted verification contract or applicable authority below. A mechanism's name alone proves neither a defect nor permission for a new product guarantee.

Use the compiled map again against the frozen candidate. Account for every criterion, contract and authorization basis, mandatory verification entry, coverage record, and lifecycle sibling. Every piece of blocking review feedback must cite one accepted owner or applicable reviewed repository rule. Classify anything else as a brief omission, authority contradiction, unresolved product decision, or new capability. Compare the architecture declaration with the final diff, requiring the named authority change in the same candidate when it is `update-required`. Re-run the material-limitation classification against the implementation so a newly exposed cutoff, fallback, security assumption, scale boundary, or foundational workaround cannot enter through generic authority; an unaccepted finding stops only its affected work and returns to the owning task for scope correction or a product decision.

When an exact accepted checkpoint package is supplied, treat its evidence as historical claims rather than a blanket waiver. Give every family one complete disposition:

- **Reused:** the owner, assumptions, neighboring contracts, and consumers remain unchanged, and the reviewer names that relationship basis.
- **Revalidated:** the owner or behavior changed, so the relevant source and check were rerun against the current candidate.
- **Stale:** a changed shared boundary, assumption, neighbor, or consumer invalidates the older observation even when the selected file hash is unchanged; reread the affected relationship before deciding its current disposition.

For correction review, independently compare the caller-selected return receipt candidate and the candidate identified in current `review.md` with the current candidate. The receipt preserves the historical candidate and reason; the review file is mutable and is not linked to that receipt. Stop without a verdict if either required identity is absent, cannot be resolved, has no comparison range, or diverges. Resolve every prior finding and return one complete disposition rather than silently dropping findings or repeating the whole semantic audit without cause.

# Review and repository disposition

Use this section for commissioning or processing review, correction, brief replacement, integration, repository cleanup or completion. The [main conversation core](#route-common-requests) owns human authority, product status, review-actor language and replies. Use [the shared runtime contract](#coding-agent-runtime-adapters) for exact request contracts and the selected runtime instructions inline, for native launch.

Known item and attempt identities use exact item status, definition, attempt inspection and the required authority/evidence reads. Do not preload overview; board-wide discovery follows [bounded discovery](#bounded-discovery) only when the requested decision needs it.

## Coordinate review responsibility and checkout use

For a human-owned PR whose author is not a Pinboard worker, use `pinboard_pr_review` on its ready item. Record a canonical brief tied to the current definition, exact requirement sources, expected behavior, consumers, owners, PR, and applicable repository criteria. Have a different task review that brief before recording a round. The coding harness supplies each full observed PR commit and observation source; Pinboard does not verify remote freshness or hosted checks. Record every round against that observation with findings, verification limits, and a disposition for each prior finding. Report the findings to the human in conversation after each round, including the exact reviewed head and any unverified or newer observed head. If a newer head appears, review it in another round or ask the human whether to stop at the earlier reviewed head. Close only on explicit human direction, including when no round was completed. Preserve residual concerns and any observed but unreviewed head in the final record and report; when no round was completed, say explicitly that no PR head was reviewed. Review-only work uses no implementation attempt, worker lease, candidate submission, or ordinary close, defer, block, resume, or replacement action. Definition revision makes the prior brief stale until it is prepared and reviewed again.

Route frozen candidates to the task that owns the outcome, not by conversational ancestry. When the recorded owner session is unavailable and the human asks a session that inherited its work to continue, that session owns the outcome under [inherited sessions](#inherited-sessions). That task commissions one fresh-context, candidate-read-only review subagent after the candidate is stable. The result returns automatically, and the owning task processes the complete accept-or-correct verdict. Keep the reviewer independent, commission one reviewer by default, and do not duplicate the full review or add reviewers without a concrete risk.

Under an active implementation request, commission this review and dispatch its in-scope corrections without asking for general reviewer approval. An explicit pause or an unresolved scope, capability, access, integration or closure decision retains its separate boundary. Recover a lost review-job response or failed pre-verification launch through [fresh launch-response recovery](#recover-a-worker-or-reviewer-launch-response); stop an invalid launch and use the new exact recipe in a fresh context.

If a Pinboard-managed pull request was published before local review, inspect the actual attempt before reporting delivery. A published PR supplies neither a protected candidate nor review evidence. For an active attempt without a candidate, dispatch or continue a worker that verifies the exact local candidate, updates `result.md`, and submits it through its own lease. For a paused attempt with stale accepted scope or Git lineage, publish a replacement brief and rebind the same attempt before selecting its legal resume action. Then inspect the protected candidate and commission the separate reviewer through `pinboard_review_job`. If any state transition, worker authority, or reviewer capability is unavailable, preserve the pending attempt and report that exact blocker. The ordinary sequence still reviews the protected candidate before repository disposition.

For a correction, require the current `result.md` to map the exact prior findings, intervening candidate delta, affected owner-consumer relationships, and each evidence family as reused, revalidated, or stale. Every semantic reread or verification rerun needs the changed relationship or accepted widening reason that requires it. The outcome owner checks this map before rendering the correction review job, and the reviewer reports the same dispositions while still returning one complete verdict. An unchanged source hash does not preserve evidence whose owner-consumer relationship changed.

Before commissioning review, inspect the attempt continuation and call `pinboard_review_job` with exact roots and a structured review leaf containing `attempt_id` and `candidate_revision`. Use `kind: initial` without histories, `package-initial` with `checkpoint_history_id`, `correction` with `correction_history_id`, or `package-correction` with both. Before supplying a package history, run `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard validate --json` separately and stop on failure. Copy exact same-attempt history identities from checkpoint output, an explicit project export, or the selected return receipt; neither is discovered automatically. Only canonical `return-for-correction/v1` reason input can supply correction context. Current nonempty `review.md` remains independently bound to its render-time digest, and may describe a newer candidate than a selected package. Give the fresh reviewer only the returned native envelope. Its direct prompt contains the exact published task and complete accepted brief; follow its interface-owned verifier to confirm provenance rather than fetching a second instruction source. The job binds the exact protected snapshot, accepted brief owner and digest, nonempty `result.md`, and selected historical bytes. The reviewer verifies every selected byte and Git identity, compares each historical candidate independently, reuses unchanged owner relationships, revalidates changed relationships and documentation, classifies unreviewed changed surfaces, and marks relationship-invalidated evidence stale despite unchanged source hashes. Widen only for architecture, persistence, wire, lifecycle, dynamic-consumer, or demonstrated-blind-spot conditions. Stop without a verdict if an identity, comparison, classification, or required widening cannot be resolved. Publication may change immutable-artifact, accepted-reference, and ledger surfaces; it neither runs full validation nor mutates lifecycle, authority, or native tasks. The outcome owner applies the reviewed result.

After a favorable reviewer verdict, call the `record-ready` review leaf with the exact candidate revision, candidate-snapshot digest, accepted-brief digest, current `result.md` and `review.md` digests, `reviewer_prompt_sha256` copied from the `prompt_reference.sha256` that the review job returned for this exact candidate and `result.md`, the task identity of the reviewer launched from that prompt, `verdict: ready`, and nonempty acceptance evidence; it has no runtime or background fields and launches nothing. `REVIEWER_PROMPT_NOT_COMMISSIONED` means no reviewer prompt was published for that subject—for example `result.md` changed after the launch—so run the review job for the current candidate first, then record the verdict of the reviewer it launched. On every later resume, inspect with fresh reconciliation observations. Missing or invalid ready identity selects review first; otherwise target-stale selects refresh, residual or diverged selects correction, the first denied or unknown required effect in source-checkout, shared-work-root, git-metadata order selects permission recovery, pending candidates select repository disposition, integrated cleanup selects repository cleanup, and integrated terminal selects completion. A favorably reviewed working-tree candidate may become a clean commit without another review when Pinboard verifies the recorded branch, the snapshot's accepted-base correlation, and a binary diff from its preimage to current HEAD matching the original snapshot under the [index-header comparison](../../../ARCHITECTURE.md#immutable-artifacts). Original accepted bytes, digests and candidate identity stay exact. This proves local code identity only; revalidate changed accepted semantics or reviewed owner-consumer relationships before reusing the review. A mismatch requires proportionate correction or review of the current candidate, and an unreadable Git observation blocks disposition with its exact read failure. Follow only the returned operation.

Use the selected runtime instructions inline, for the native fresh-reviewer launch and wait operations. The exact review job and review responsibility remain shared.

Do not use or wake another coding-agent task to review or receive the same outcome. Dispatching work, clarifying or widening scope, or sending a prior message does not establish current responsibility. A separate task owns a genuinely independent outcome and reports in its own conversation; it is never a subordinate return path.

If the runtime adapter establishes that the current runtime cannot create a subagent, keep the exact candidate in review, preserve the durable result and accepted brief, and state that review is waiting for a runtime with subagent capability. Do not create or wake a user-owned task, return routine ownership to a parent task, substitute the implementer as reviewer, or imply that the human must review unless the human explicitly chooses that route.

### Recover after a brief replacement

When an accepted brief is replaced while a returned candidate still awaits correction, its old correction request is historical context, not authority for the new target. This recovery does not apply to ordinary initial briefs, new checkpoints, or rebinds without an outstanding superseded correction.

1. Bind the replacement brief.
2. For a cross-boundary replacement, independently assess the complete current canonical brief against current authority bytes and the actual current candidate binding on its accepted base, including every moved, removed and newly added authority. Read `pinboard_return_context` with exact roots, attempt, and `selection: {kind: historical, return_history_id: <selected original return>}`. Verify its exact original receipt, accepted returned snapshot and canonical reason separately as historical context; a genuine rebase may change the current base and candidate without changing those original bytes. While the attempt is active and its latest return is historical after rebind, use `pinboard_dispatch` with `kind: replacement-readiness`, its fresh project dispatch receipt, exact checkpoint, `review_id`, selected `correction_history_id`, full `pinboard-correction-source-review/v1` as `brief_review`, and `current_candidate` naming the assessed commit or complete working-tree identity. The source review binds the current full canonical contract review, historical accepted snapshot and reason, and a concrete independent source assessment for the current candidate. This establishes replacement-brief readiness; reserve the complete implementation verdict for the protected candidate review in step 4. Pass no environment or prompt.
3. Verify the returned proof and plain ready-review identities, then protect the returned `candidate_revision` using your own current attempt authority. The proof binds the historical review context and assessed current candidate; plain readiness belongs to the replacement brief and is consumed independently by checkpoint acceptance. Publication verifies current sources and accepted binding, rechecks the exact current candidate after each publication, and produces no worker prompt, launch, lease or lifecycle mutation. Identical bytes reuse; differing evidence preserves collision evidence. After a committed partial failure, inspect the named surfaces and current continuation rather than replaying the operation. Local replacements keep their existing preparation rules.
4. Commission one fresh complete implementation review against the replacement brief and protected current candidate. Supply the selected previous return and checkpoint as independently verified historical context. Retain every prior finding with an evidence-backed disposition; replacing the brief does not erase findings or make the old verdict current.
5. Preserve the complete new verdict. If it requests changes, apply one new `return-for-correction` and retain its actual canonical history identity.
6. Independently review the current correction sources, then dispatch correction using that new return on the same reviewed brief binding. Preserve the accepted plain readiness record through corrected submission, review, and checkpoint acceptance. If another genuine brief replacement becomes necessary, repeat fresh review against it rather than transferring the old verdict.

Review-job may select an older return as context; correction dispatch requires the current canonical return. Do not replay completed transitions, relax stale-return checks, or add storage machinery to preserve the old request.

The responsible task reviews the frozen candidate, then applies the review outcome through the state-appropriate project transition. Use `complete:<attempt>` only when the human has authorized the entire work-item outcome and its named completion boundary is satisfied, the current v4 checkpoint disposition is `terminal`, the exact candidate is protected and independently reviewed, and every already-authorized repository disposition and cleanup effect has succeeded; keep a favorable final candidate in review while those effects run. When an independently buildable checkpoint is accepted and the canonical brief disposition is `continue`, use `accept-checkpoint:<attempt>` with the stable checkpoint ID, exact candidate identity, and review evidence written as a [human-read record](#write-human-read-records); it archives the exact current `result.md` and `review.md`, pauses the same item and attempt, and fences worker authority. Publish the revised canonical JSON brief at its next artifact revision, then use the ordinary `resume:<item>` with that accepted reference before dispatch. When the protected candidate is accepted but accepted checkpoint work remains within the same active attempt, use `accept-review-and-continue:<attempt>` with that exact candidate identity and acceptance evidence written as a [human-read record](#write-human-read-records); it returns the item and attempt to active, clears the protected candidate, records the accepted candidate and evidence without a checkpoint, sets the next action to continue, and fences the previous worker authority. When review finds an actionable defect, use `return-for-correction:<attempt>` with a reason written as a [human-read record](#write-human-read-records) that identifies the durable review evidence, and capture the successful transition's exact `history_id`. Select project dispatch again and commission a fresh independent source review—bound to the accepted brief for a local checkpoint, or to the effective checkpoint and its current contract review for a cross-boundary one—and pass it with the selected return to the matching correction dispatch leaf before launching the fresh correction worker. The same attempt and evidence remain; the new worker reacquires at a higher generation through the rooted MCP calls in its generated prompt.

Treat the paused state produced by an accepted intermediate checkpoint as an internal evidence boundary when the human has already authorized continued execution, the brief records remaining work, and no blocker or unresolved human-owned decision exists. Report the accepted milestone, then continue the owning turn through any already-selected repository disposition, next brief publication and binding, resume, fresh worker acquisition, and delivery. Preserve the pause, immutable evidence archive, and authority fence; stop only for an explicit request to pause, a genuine blocker, missing authority, or an unresolved human-owned decision.

## Review and completion

Before terminal completion, identify the human's actual whole-item completion instruction and verify that its named boundary is satisfied. Reuse an earlier explicit instruction when it still applies; do not ask again merely because review or repository effects have since finished. If the instruction makes completion conditional on a merge, keep the item nonterminal until that condition is verified. A knowingly selected isolated result can be the final outcome without a merge.

Candidate readiness and human terminal authority answer separate questions. A terminal brief, favorable review, draft publication, no remaining code work, or an acknowledgment such as “this step is done” supplies no missing whole-item decision. Keep remaining accepted work within the same item; do not reclassify it as follow-ups to manufacture completion. Use checkpoint acceptance or reviewed continuation when their accepted work remains. Continue already-authorized same-item work through its checkpoint route without another general approval.

A merge report, close, cleanup, or completion instruction never waives, retires, or defers remaining accepted work, and it is not by itself late direction that changes accepted semantics: after “it's merged, you can close,” the current checkpoint's remaining work still belongs to the item. Dropping that work takes the human's explicit decision about the named work, asked after you state what dropping it means, before any definition revision, cancellation, or completion that would drop it. Until then, keep the current definition and brief, report the remaining work as what keeps the item open, and continue or offer its existing checkpoint route. This rule is distinct from releasing an acceptance gate you introduced yourself.

Record the human's exact completion words through the currently advertised native completion contract: use `human_decision` when it declares that field, otherwise preserve the words in its declared evidence field. Source instructions describing a newer field do not change an installed callable or authorize installation. If the advertised contract cannot represent a required condition, report that exact gap; do not invent a field or another execution route. If no applicable instruction exists or its boundary remains unsatisfied, report that precise pending decision or condition before completion. The text records attribution within Pinboard's trusted-local boundary; it does not authenticate the human or prove the meaning of their words. Supplying it relaxes no commissioned-review, terminal-disposition, replacement or freshness condition.

Keep a favorably reviewed candidate protected while read-only investigation or explicit retention settles the existing accepted work. Record that decision in separate private evidence and cite it in completion evidence. Preserve the accepted brief and the bound result and review bytes. Use `accept-review-and-continue` only when accepted checkpoint work remains; it clears candidate protection and requires another submission. A material change to any accepted worker deliverable or acceptance requirement follows the complete definition-and-brief replacement route below and requires review of the new exact candidate. A newly required investigation or report can change accepted scope even when source code is unchanged.

Treat a refused closure as a bounded diagnosis. Report the actual accepted remaining work or missing current candidate, review, or evidence, then follow its focused inspection to establish what remains. Closure does not authorize reconstructing a candidate or launching implementation. Keep already-cleared or rebound history as history; it supplies no current approval. Reuse a valid current commissioned ready review when its exact candidate and evidence still satisfy completion.

Retired patch-only working-tree v1 snapshots remain exact readable/exportable terminal bytes under independently verified archive source, receipt and definition closure. They provide no restoration, integration, review or correction authority. Current complete commit v1, working-tree v2 and declared v3 snapshots retain their exact independent checks and correction-context formats; retired checkpoint v2 packages retain exact non-executable patch-only terminal history under independent certificate closure.

For a reviewed candidate whose starting checkout still matches its returned snapshot, call `pinboard_correction_context` with the exact attempt and return history ID before commissioning the independent source reviewer. Supply the returned effective brief, reviewed-authority identities and hashes, canonical reason, accepted starting candidate identity, and coverage-reuse eligibility to that reviewer. If the accepted brief, every reviewed source, and accepted ready review are unchanged, a cross-boundary reviewer makes a fresh candidate-bound assessment in `ReusedCoverageCorrectionReview` and dispatch uses `reuse-correction`. A reported blocker selects the full `CorrectionSourceReview` and `correction` route. A local reviewer uses `LocalCorrectionSourceReview`. Dispatch recomputes and rechecks these identities. Report a blocker and its next supported action without repeating unchanged status. An earlier ready review or a different starting snapshot cannot replace the fresh correction assessment. Substituting a different host application still requires its own human approval.

When tracked changes or new untracked names have drifted from a current returned checkout, use `pinboard_return_context` with `selection: {kind: current-candidate, return_history_id: <current return>}`. Give the reviewer its plain `review_context` and exact `current_candidate` binding. A fresh independent assessment must explain the drift and bind the observed tracked candidate plus omitted path names. Dispatch uses `kind: candidate-correction` and a strict `pinboard-current-correction-source-review/v1` wrapper: `boundary: cross-boundary` carries a full `CorrectionSourceReview` in `source_review`; `boundary: local` carries a `LocalCorrectionSourceReview`. Both carry the exact `current_candidate` record. Valid unchanged evidence may inform that assessment, but the existing `reuse-correction` leaf remains an exact-return route. Candidate-bound correction permits reviewed diff and path drift while retaining the returned branch, HEAD, accepted base and current return. It neither includes omitted bytes in identity nor turns a historical return after rebind into correction authority. Reobserve and reassess a changed binding; after committed publication failure, inspect effects before any continuation.

When hosted CI finds an ordinary implementation defect after a draft PR was published, continue correction in the same attempt through a fresh candidate submission and separate review. If repository publication of the corrected commit is already authorized, update the same draft PR and verify hosted checks on that exact head. Ask the human only for an actual missing repository authorization or a material product, architecture, compatibility, scope, or risk decision; routine correction within the accepted brief needs no new decision.

Report repository publication and local review as separate facts, naming review as not started, underway, favorable, blocked, or returned for correction from fresh attempt state and actual reviewer evidence. A published PR makes review neither favorable nor the item complete. If the human explicitly chooses to proceed before review, name that choice and keep the review pending. A locally matching protected commit verifies no remote PR, push, merge, or hosted-CI head; apply the review-provenance rule in [the human's picture](#keep-the-humans-picture-current).

For an agent-authored Pinboard PR, create or keep it draft while any accepted agent-side work remains, including implementation checkpoints, corrections, independent review, and required hosted checks. If an existing ready PR needs an unfinished new head, convert it to draft and verify the remote draft state before pushing that head; if conversion cannot be confirmed, hold the push and report the blocker. Continue authorized corrections on the same draft PR.

After every accepted agent-side step is complete, observe the PR's current remote head and confirm that independent review and every required check cover that exact head. Then mark the draft PR ready for human review and verify its state and head again. If the head changed or coverage cannot be confirmed, keep or return the PR to draft and continue the missing work. A push, green CI result, or locally reviewed candidate alone does not trigger readiness. Pinboard does not certify remote head or hosted checks; the outcome owner reports the observations, and the human retains the merge decision.

At publication, check, review, and wrap-up updates, briefly name the PR's draft state, the agent work still pending, and the planned ready transition. Once it is ready, name the observed head and its review and required-check coverage, leaving the merge to the human. Report hosted checks and remote state as unverified when they were not observed.

Before commissioning a caller-selected checkpoint review, require accepted candidate bytes as well as the package reference. A current v3 package carries a portable canonical snapshot with its actual preimage and exact diff. Retired v1/v2 packages are non-executable terminal archive history; selecting them rejects before prompt publication. Keep current v3 package review and current restoration independent of archive membership. Historical patch assurance cannot authorize a new complete-state correction start.

Checkpoint acceptance for a new candidate verifies its protected identity before publishing candidate, result, implementation review, and the v3 package as one evidence closure. A working-tree candidate binds the actual full HEAD revision and exact full-index `git diff --binary --full-index HEAD` bytes; a commit candidate binds the full current HEAD with a clean working tree and the exact full-index `git diff --binary --full-index <accepted-brief-base> <current-HEAD>` bytes. Validation, review, project export, and covered completion stop when the current package's candidate reference, identity, or canonical bytes are missing or mismatched. Retired patch-only working-tree v1 snapshots remain non-executable terminal history under verified archive closure. Retired checkpoint v2 bytes and captured labels keep exact patch-only assurance under independent certificate closure; full commit labels establish no complete preimage.

Treat worker completion as a review request, not acceptance. Compare the attempt brief, diff or commit, result receipt, and fresh proportionate verification. Start with the changed and explicitly uncertain semantic surface: reuse unchanged reviewed relationships, revalidate changed relationships and documentation, and classify every changed file or contract preparation did not cover. Widen only for architecture, persistence, wire, lifecycle, dynamic-consumer, or demonstrated-blind-spot evidence, not merely because the checkpoint is cross-boundary. Check the architecture declaration against the final owner and dependency-direction diff: `none` must be truthful, `read-only` must conform to its named authority, and `update-required` must include a coherent same-candidate authority change. Account for every acceptance criterion, Contract row and authorization basis, coverage row, and lifecycle sibling row. When the brief carries a requirement from the readiness hook, verify its affected capability and proportionate evidence against the recorded project tier or equivalent policy. Without that policy the hook remains non-blocking; separately accepted readiness obligations retain their own basis under the general assurance rule. Apply the brief-composition rule without adding retroactive guarantees.
