When the checkpoint invokes the [developer-navigation lens](#trace-developer-navigation), verify the final representative trace, sibling edit sites, retained exhaustive owners, and dynamic-wiring failure mode against the frozen candidate. Apply the [assurance classification](#keep-assurance-inside-accepted-product-scope): every blocking finding cites accepted scope or an exact brief contract or criterion, an applicable repository rule, an exact reviewed product-authority family, a named production consumer, or an observed supported-path failure, never broad correctness prose, an exploratory failure, public narrative, or newly written guidance. Fix defects and enforce accepted hardening without redundant confirmation, and route a materially broader unsupported guarantee to the [one human assurance decision](#keep-assurance-inside-accepted-product-scope). Classify each finding as an implementation defect, brief omission, authority contradiction, product decision, or new capability. A correction review may reuse package evidence only when its owner and relevant relationships remain valid; it revalidates changed owners, marks relationship-invalidated neighbors stale even with unchanged hashes, and resolves every prior finding before one complete verdict. Complete the item only when every acceptance criterion is satisfied and current knowledge owners are reconciled. A `continue` checkpoint may be accepted or returned to active reviewed work, never terminally completed. A `terminal` checkpoint may complete only from protected review with the exact candidate, current result and review digests, independent reviewer identity, and one ascending compact reused-or-revalidated row for every enumerated checkpoint, including an empty row set when none was previously accepted. Pinboard refuses completion with `CANDIDATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, unchanged and before publishing any completion evidence, unless it holds a ready review recorded through `record-ready` for that exact candidate, snapshot, brief, `result.md` and `review.md`, commissioned by a reviewer prompt `pinboard_review_job` published for that subject, and naming the same `reviewer_task_id` as the completion. Never choose or invent a reviewer identity. If the required record is absent, report the missing review and inspect the exact round before offering its commissioned review route; the closure warning itself launches nothing. Follow the review procedure above only with review authority, then complete with the recorded reviewer's identity. A retained `pinboard-candidate-review/v1` record carries no commission link and does not count; commission one new review. Focused completion supplies the installed native tool's strict reviewed input; follow that exact advertised contract and record the human's completion words as required above. Broad action discovery intentionally omits completion. Original v2/v3 briefs are historical-only facts for independently verified archive, checkpoint and completion bindings; they have no operational decoding or recovery route. Pinboard rechecks the same accepted brief reference and disposition under lock before publication and commit.

When an authorized repository disposition includes creating or updating a pull request, use `$technical-writing` in quiet editorial mode for its description. Ground the description in the accepted definition and brief, the exact candidate and diff, implementation evidence, verification, and the accepted review. Make the requested outcome recognizable before implementation detail. Preserve material caveats and unknowns, and do not interview the user when those sources already determine truthful content.

Also compare the frozen candidate with the project's current limitations and the brief's recorded assessment. Reject a candidate that introduces, widens, preserves, masks, or deepens an unacknowledged material limitation, even under generic implementation authority or behind a locally correct compensating layer. A newly accepted or materially changed limitation is bound to the current definition and existing brief provenance, represented as a cross-boundary contract with `update-required` architecture impact and complete coverage, and reflected in the named current-truth owner, without another brief field or consent receipt. A missing decision is a brief omission or unresolved product decision, never worker discretion.

The owning task owns review publication: after the candidate-read-only reviewer returns a complete verdict, write it to the active attempt's `review.md`, then link its purpose before announcing or applying acceptance, return for correction, checkpoint acceptance, accept-review-and-continue, or terminal completion. Later mentions follow the readable-artifact rule; do not link immutable copies archived by acceptance transitions.

### Reconcile late direction and replace the definition and brief

Before presenting a candidate, accepting review, offering repository disposition, or wrapping up, account for every user direction and repository change after the current accepted brief or exact candidate was established. Distinguish work that implements the current brief from a change to accepted semantics. When semantics changed, do not present, submit, accept, or complete against the superseded identity: replace the complete item definition, publish a matching canonical brief, rebind the active or paused attempt to that current scope and its accepted Git lineage, produce a new exact candidate, and obtain a new exact-candidate review.

When the human adds direction while a worker is active, compare it with the complete accepted brief. A clarification already covered by the brief may go directly to the same worker. A new material requirement changes accepted semantics: do not send it as implementation authority or wait for `result.md` to reconcile it. Preserve the worker's evidence, replace the complete item definition and matching canonical brief, and rebind the active attempt before another candidate submission. Rebind fences the old worker's Pinboard authority but does not stop its native process: stop it through its native handle or wait for it to finish, and confirm it no longer writes to the checkout before dispatching a fresh worker there, leaving dispatch pending if that cannot be confirmed. Then continue through supported dispatch and fresh worker authority against the revised brief, and obtain a new exact-candidate review.

Use the lifecycle route that matches the current state. Before submission, revision makes the active attempt stale: publish the matching brief and rebind it, keeping it active. While a candidate is in review—even after a favorable verdict—return it for correction with a reason saying accepted scope superseded it rather than that the implementation is defective, then revise, publish, rebind, implement, submit, and review again. After `accept-review-and-continue` returned the attempt to active, revise, publish, and rebind without a review-state return. A paused attempt follows the same publication and rebind path while staying paused, even when live dependencies keep resume unavailable. After terminal completion, preserve its history and treat later direction as new work.

Distinguish a genuine scope change that supersedes the candidate from a human request merely to pause, hold, sequence or wait on another item, save state, or switch sessions or models while an attempt is in `review` or `active`. `pause` is only legal from `active`, and running `return-for-correction`, `revise-item`, or `pause` on a reviewed candidate clears `protected_candidate_revision`, invalidates any ready review record, and forces replacement-brief, rebind, and re-review ceremony. When accepted product scope has not changed and the human asks to pause, hold, or sequence an item in a way that would invalidate a reviewed candidate or force a costly `return-for-correction`, `revise-item`, rebind, or re-review ceremony, warn the human before mutating state and recommend waiting in place instead. Briefly explain how durable `ready`, `active`, and `review` state works on disk across sessions, models, and runtimes and what to expect when resuming in the same or another session or model (continuation picks up directly from the preserved review or attempt state without re-running review); mutate state only if the human confirms after that warning or when accepted scope genuinely changed.

When acceptance requires exact-head CI, resolve the needed commit and publication authority early enough to follow the single-pass candidate sequence described here: prepare the commit before submission, then publish it unchanged after favorable review and verify its CI before acceptance. Otherwise, repository disposition may follow candidate acceptance. Keep code acceptance, Pinboard state, commit state, branch integration, remote publication, and deliberate deferral distinct. Before asking the human to wrap up, refresh only the decision-relevant facts: review outcome; dirty or committed state; current branch and checkout or worktree; intended target; known filename overlap or conflict risk; and remote delivery status when it affects the choice. State observations, uncertainty, and limitations. A separate worktree avoids competing writes in one checkout but does not make later integration conflict-free.

When repository disposition remains unresolved, recommend the best-supported next action with alternatives whose repository effects are explicit, using the [question presentation](#match-detail-to-the-question) with two to four choices. When remote publication is available, include `commit the candidate, push its branch, and open a draft PR` beside any useful commit-only, named-branch integration, or publication choices, without implying the draft-PR path is required, and perform only the selected action. Unless the agreed outcome keeps the work isolated, do not routinely offer leaving it unchanged, uncommitted, isolated, or for later; acknowledge an explicit request to defer. Otherwise the choice stays on the `Still open:` line until the human chooses a concrete disposition.

### Repository disposition and local closure

At the repository decision, state the human's exact choice and the remaining sequence: verify the selected disposition, perform only authorized cleanup, then apply the authorized terminal transition. Offer one bundled decision when its exact targets and consequences are established. Each named effect has separate authority; execute the selected sequence in order and verify each effect before advancing. A merge or green checks alone authorizes no deletion or completion. If an effect fails or remains uncertain, stop before later destructive or terminal effects and report completed and pending facts separately.

For explicit local-only closure of an already favorably reviewed candidate, carry out the named effects through this bounded path. Attribute a human-reported merge to the human and verify the local relation needed for cleanup or completion; that report needs no GitHub or merge-actor investigation. An excluded installation and a difference between source guidance and the advertised native contract create no version-audit prerequisite. Keep the protected candidate and its bound brief, result and review bytes unchanged. Reuse observations within the same closure sequence while their decision-relevant facts remain current; reread after a relevant effect, changed target, evidence change, occupancy change, stale receipt or failed observation. This reuse never replaces fresh action selection or the executable's locked rechecks.

1. Read exact item status and inspect the named attempt with `reconciliation: null`. A current `ready` verdict and `reconcile-repository` mean the exact candidate already has commissioned review; reuse it despite the board state `review`. If current coverage is missing or invalid, retain the worktree and branches and report the missing review before any cleanup or completion: unresolved review still uses the worktree. Follow [review and completion](#review-and-completion) only with review authority. Close intent supplies neither review commissioning nor candidate reconstruction authority.
2. Resolve the intended local target and read item-status operation `integration` once for that target. `content-present` supports `candidate-integrated` with the returned `target_revision`, including rebase and squash integration. Preserve the original review subject; this proves neither review of surrounding commits nor remote freshness. `content-not-present`, `no-change` or a failed read is inconclusive: establish the actual relation before cleanup or completion. Do not infer another relation, create an empty PR or broadly rereview unchanged code. A local-only instruction adds no fetch, push, PR, hosted-check or remote-deletion effect.
3. If cleanup was requested or authorized, establish the exact worktree and applicable branch targets against the verified integration target. Read worker authority for this attempt and establish the cleanup conditions below, including other task or attempt occupancy and needed work outside the protected candidate's diff. The positive integration check covers only that reviewed diff; an unknown or failed condition leaves requested cleanup and completion pending. If cleanup was neither requested nor authorized, retain those targets and proceed to the terminal phase when the other completion conditions hold.
4. Inspect with `candidate-integrated`, the verified target revision and the phase/effect observations below. Use `cleanup` only for required cleanup; use `terminal` after cleanup succeeds or when none is required. Follow the returned continuation. A denied or unknown required effect selects permission recovery; an observation describes current authority and capability, never grants it.
5. For authorized cleanup whose conditions all hold, remove the exact disposable worktree, then its local branch, then any explicitly authorized still-present remote branch. Verify each effect before advancing; an already absent branch is no remaining deletion effect. Use a surviving checkout for subsequent repository calls. After cleanup, inspect the terminal phase with current observations; refresh only facts the cleanup changed or made uncertain.
6. Request the exact fresh project `complete` action, fill its current completion contract with the human's exact completion decision, protected candidate and recorded reviewer's identity, and apply it only under explicit completion authority. The contract preserves commissioned-review bindings, accepted terminal scope and checkpoint coverage. Follow the returned effect and retry disposition; do not replay a committed or uncertain effect. Immediately before the closing reply, read exact item status as required by [wrap-up](#wrap-up-with-facts). Report local integration and terminal status as distinct facts. When the requested effects and terminal status are verified, end the turn without more tool work, investigation or proposed follow-ups; an unverified remote actor or excluded installation is no remaining work.

Reconciliation always contains exactly three effect observations in `source-checkout`, `shared-work-root`, `git-metadata` order. For the integrated local closure path:

| Phase | `source-checkout` | `shared-work-root` | `git-metadata` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cleanup` | observed required status | `not-required` | observed required status |
| `terminal` | `not-required` | observed required status | `not-required` |

An observed required status is exactly `allowed`, `denied` or `unknown`. Supply `not-required` only where the phase requires no effect, even if that resource is writable. In particular, `shared-work-root: allowed` is invalid for cleanup. The [runtime request contract](#current-mcp-request-shapes) owns the full native input shape and other reconciliation routes.

Cleanup requires all of these facts:

- no active coding-agent task or Pinboard attempt uses the worktree;
- no needed uncommitted changes remain in it;
- no needed branch commits are absent from the accepted integration target;
- the worktree and each applicable local or remote branch target are exact; and
- the human explicitly authorized deletion of each applicable target.

A review-state attempt with no live worker authority no longer uses its isolated worktree once its exact favorably reviewed candidate is present at the verified integration target. Retained lineage and protected evidence alone do not block removal. An active attempt, live worker, unintegrated candidate or unresolved review still uses it; another occupant remains a separate condition. When requested cleanup fails a condition or leaves it unknown, retain the worktree and branches, leave the item nonterminal and name the evidence or decision needed next. Close intent alone authorizes no cleanup. When cleanup is neither requested nor authorized, deletion authority is no prerequisite to otherwise authorized completion.

If the human already authorized the exact cleanup and completion sequence, execute it in the same turn without another routine confirmation. Ask only for a missing effect authority. Do not manufacture integration or publication as a prerequisite when the human knowingly accepts another disposition; use that disposition's supported reconciliation route instead of this already-integrated local path.

For an accepted intermediate checkpoint, use the checkpoint acceptance path above. Its paused item and attempt remain nonterminal, checkpoint evidence remains immutable under the same attempt, and terminal item history remains absent until a later full-outcome completion. For an accepted intermediate review inside an unfinished checkpoint, use `accept-review-and-continue:<attempt>` instead; it records the passing review without accepting the checkpoint and leaves the fenced attempt ready to continue after a worker reacquires it.

Use `return-for-correction:<attempt>` for an implementation defect against an accepted owner or when newly accepted semantics supersede the protected review candidate. In the second case, record scope supersession rather than calling the implementation defective, then follow the [complete definition-and-brief replacement route](#reconcile-late-direction-and-replace-the-definition-and-brief). For a brief omission, authority contradiction, unresolved product decision, or new capability that has not become accepted scope, preserve the review evidence and stop before any lifecycle transition until the existing upstream owner resolves it; do not turn the review feedback into implementation scope or invent a state, transition, or alternate acceptance path. For an implementation defect, record the exact correction reason instead of completing the item, manufacturing a new attempt, or editing lifecycle files. Report the outcome compactly with the reason's lead sentence only: `Returned for correction — <lead sentence>; the same attempt and review evidence are preserved and ready for a named worker to reacquire. No acceptance occurred.` If the executable does not offer that action for a valid review return, preserve the review evidence and report the workflow blocker; do not bypass the missing transition.

# Parallel Work

Use this workflow for requests such as:

- “What can run independently right now?”
- “Let me choose a batch from the safe work.”
- “Launch all safe work in parallel.”

Do not use it merely because more than one item exists. Ordinary next-work selection uses [status and selection](#status-and-selection).

Use [the shared runtime adapters](#coding-agent-runtime-adapters) and the selected runtime instructions inline, for native task, subagent, worktree, permission, and waiting operations. This reference owns only the shared selection and launch decisions.

## Build the preview

1. Require authority `sqlite-v11`.
2. Call `pinboard_parallel_preview` with exact roots and `selection: all-safe` inside `request`. This explicit leaf spans current portfolio facts and exact checkpoint dependency matches without proposal bodies or scans of retained history; do not include `item_ids`.
3. Present the result in two compact groups:
   - **Ready together:** the unambiguous all-safe set.
   - **Not ready:** excluded items with the command's exact reason translated into ordinary language.
4. Make every item label a native clickable link to its confirmed item view under the shared policy’s readable-artifact rule.
5. Add one execution-form recommendation to every launchable item:
   - Use a **Subagent** for bounded work that belongs to the current outcome and should return to its owning task. Keep design, refinement, new-authority, live-application, external-write, and likely user-input decisions in the owning task until the work has a complete accepted brief, an independently buildable checkpoint, and already-authorized permissions.
   - Use a **Separate task** only for a genuinely independent outcome that the human intends to follow in that task's own conversation. It is not a subordinate worker and does not return its result to the current task.
6. Explain the recommendation in one short phrase and identify the task the human should follow. Do not recommend a separate task merely because work is incomplete, interactive, approval-sensitive, or structurally independent.

If the request was only to list or preview, stop after presenting the groups. A read-only preview is not launch permission.

Use each returned dependency's target and acceptance status. An accepted checkpoint can unlock a consumer while its producer continues; a whole-item target still waits for completion or supersession. Keep whole-item serialization when a scarce resource must remain exclusive through the producer's remaining work. These conditions change structural eligibility, not batch or launch authority.

## Resolve batch authority

Treat either of these as explicit launch authority:

- the user names an exact subset from the preview;
- the user says to launch all safe work.

“All safe” means the preview's **Ready together** group.

Before creating anything, call `pinboard_parallel_preview` again with exact roots, `selection: selected`, and every authorized item in nonempty unique `item_ids`, all inside `request`. This leaf reads only those current items and their direct launch constraints:

```text
{"request":{"project_root":"<exact checkout>","work_root":"<exact work root>","selection":"selected","item_ids":["<first>","<second>"]}}
```

Proceed only when `safe` is true. Preserve its revision as the batch observation. If it is false, show the changed reason and ask only for the decision that the new state requires. Safe is structural evidence, not readiness or worker authority; the subsequent accepted brief, fresh authority and native creation checks still apply.

## Launch each outcome

Work through the authorized items in the presented order. Before each external creation, rerun the selected preview for that item and every not-yet-created item. Stop the remaining batch if structural safety changed; tasks already created remain real and must be reported.

For a **Separate task**:

1. Use the environment's native task creation capability. This is authorized by the user's exact batch request.
2. Give it the repository root, item identity, confirmed item-view link when available, and fresh preview revision, with an instruction to use Pinboard to inspect the item and apply only its own legal transitions. When its checkout or worktree must be selected, use [preparation and dispatch](#checkout-and-baseline) for project-specific baseline inference and confirmation; do not assume that a local branch named `main` is current or that any fixed remote name is authoritative.
3. Name that task as the one to follow for its outcome, as part of the shared policy’s [current-activity fact](#keep-the-humans-picture-current). It reports and requests decisions there; do not use task-to-task messaging to return its result to the current task.
4. Do not replace it with a subagent when separate-task creation is unavailable, because the human selected a separate outcome and conversation.

For a **Subagent**:

1. Keep the current task as the outcome owner and resolve incomplete, ambiguous, or interactive decisions there.
2. Follow [preparation and dispatch](#prepare-delegated-attempts), including the canonical attempt brief and exact dispatch prompt.
3. Launch it through the environment's subagent capability only after the dispatch check succeeds; its result returns automatically to the owning task.
4. If the runtime lacks subagent capability, preserve the prepared attempt and report that exact limitation. Do not create or wake a user-owned task, return routine ownership to a parent task, or silently change the selected execution form.

Task creation is an external effect, not a ledger transaction. Do not claim atomic launch or try to roll back a successfully created task because a later creation failed.

## Report the batch

Keep the report compact and exact:

| Item | Form | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| linked item label | separate task or subagent | created with task identifier, or not created with exact cause |

Link each item under the shared policy’s readable-artifact rule. Say `batch launched` only when every authorized item was created. Otherwise say `partial launch`, identify what exists, name the first changed-state or transport failure, and state whether retry needs user action. Never count a prepared prompt, retained proposal, or attempted message as a created task.

## Preview and launch independent work

When the user asks what can run in parallel, asks to choose a batch, or explicitly asks to launch independent work, follow this complete parallel-work section.

Use `pinboard_parallel_preview` as read-only structural evidence through its exact selected or all-safe request leaf. It does not certify readiness, acquire authority, authorize task creation or decide product priority. Keep these outcomes distinct:

- listing or previewing creates no tasks;
- an exact selected subset or “all safe work” is launch authority for that batch only;
- each external creation receives a fresh structural check and an explainable separate-task or subagent recommendation.

# Invocation evidence

Use this section when exact capture or a consequential Pinboard invocation anomaly needs investigation. The [main conversation core](#route-common-requests) owns concern disposition and the human picture. Capture is private evidence, never ledger authority.

### Capture and reconcile consequential invocation evidence

For an initialized project, `<work-root>/contributor-traces.config` decides whether normal Pinboard invocations are captured. The selected work root is the shared ignored `.pinboard` by default; an explicit work root keeps its own setting and traces. Its project mode is created explicitly `off`; an item override of `inherit`, `on`, or `off` changes the effective mode for that item, and the runtime rereads it before each supported CLI or MCP invocation. Effective on declares that exact arguments and results are safe to persist locally without redaction. Automatic traces are private ignored files under `<work-root>/invocation-traces/` with newest-100 retention. A ledger or lifecycle read can still initialize that local setting or publish a trace; read-only ledger behavior does not promise a non-writing filesystem invocation.

Both `pinboard_brief_sources` and `pinboard_brief_source_plan_output` bypass automatic and manual MCP capture. The former reads plans and verified batches without writing; the latter writes only its explicitly selected plan destination. Neither initializes trace settings or publishes invocation traces. Other manual capture remains available through the CLI `--capture-evidence <file> --safe-to-persist-exactly --` wrapper or a dedicated MCP `--capture-evidence-dir <existing-directory> --safe-to-persist-exactly` process, with caller-owned destination and retention and no environment snapshot. [Contributor guidance](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#diagnose-pinboard-invocations-during-contributor-work) owns setup, toggling, risk and deletion details.

Treat captured files as private evidence, not accepted ledger truth. CLI records preserve the complete launcher argv, original stdout and stderr bytes, and exit status; MCP records preserve the exact SDK-decoded arguments and strictly validated result, without transport bytes or pre-callback client events. A strict result-validation failure preserves an unavailable record with the callback classification and commit reference before the error is re-raised. Distinguish pre-publication `capture-unavailable` from `capture-committed-with-warning`, whose filename retains the published digest and size after a post-publication failure. Never replay a mutation to replace missing, interrupted or externally truncated evidence.

During any work on an enabled Pinboard project or item, investigate consequential Pinboard anomalies when they arise, regardless of the current work item or Codex task. Routine success stays quiet. Inspect the relevant trace, but report selectors and conclusions rather than raw values that may contain secrets. Reconcile evidence at a natural task or review boundary, consolidate recurrence, and keep one compact record for each distinct consequential observation with:

- attempted outcome;
- observed behavior, exact evidence selector when available, and confidence in the conclusion;
- recovery outcome;
- measured command, time or token cost when available, without inventing absent measurements;
- classification as Pinboard product behavior or discovery, evidence handling, caller or harness error, runtime or environment constraint, external client behavior, or model limitation;
- disposition and rationale;
- observable reopening condition for deferred or accepted friction.

Use one explicit disposition: fixed and verified in authorized scope; incorporated into an exact admitted item whose accepted definition covers it; admitted separately with saved priority; deferred because cost, uncertainty or an external constraint prevents a useful remedy; accepted friction with proportionate demonstrated recovery; or unresolved because evidence is insufficient. An actionable Pinboard-owned or project-owned observation is not disposed until it is fixed and verified or an exact admitted item owns it with a saved priority decision. When that ownership needs human authority, ask one admission or priority question at the existing result or review boundary instead of leaving a TODO or creating another workflow stage.

# State and recovery

Use the selected runtime instructions inline, for trusted identity and runtime-native waiting or recovery operations; [the shared runtime adapters](#handling-another-runtimes-attempt) govern an attempt another runtime started. SQLite remains the only lifecycle authority.

## Contents

- [Authoritative state](#authoritative-state)
- [Leases and revocation](#leases-and-revocation)
- [Invalid state](#invalid-state)
- [Interrupted tasks](#interrupted-tasks)
- [Inherited sessions](#inherited-sessions)

## Authoritative state

The project-local work root contains one SQLite authority and generated or immutable supporting artifacts:

```text
.pinboard/
  state.sqlite3
  artifacts/
  views/
```

Resolve the project through Git's shared common directory. A linked worktree therefore uses the primary checkout's `.pinboard`, not a competing ignored root. Default initialization adds only the anchored `/.pinboard/` entry to that shared repository's local Git exclude file; it does not edit committed ignore files or hide unrelated `.codex` content. Read only the selected initialized root; do not scan or substitute other locations. An explicit `--work-root` remains at the exact selected path.

Require `authority: sqlite-v11` from the executable. `state.sqlite3` owns lifecycle, dependencies, attempts, preparation and attempt leases, proposals, history, and accepted artifact references. `views/` is replaceable output and never a fallback authority. Do not reconstruct state from other files.

For a released `sqlite-v6`, `sqlite-v7`, `sqlite-v8`, `sqlite-v9`, or `sqlite-v10` ledger, run `pinboard migrate-schema` while quiescent to read its canonical plan and ID, then run `pinboard migrate-schema --apply <plan-id>` to retain exact predecessor bytes and apply the atomic upgrade. Current v5 plans advance exact v10 to v11, retain `.v10` bytes and add an empty indexed relation for latest decision-batch receipt references. Retained v4 plans advance v9 to v10, retain `.v9` bytes, and backfill indexed checkpoint acceptance facts from strictly decoded receipts and their exact producer attempts. Retained v3 plans advance v8 to v9 after verifying original artifact bytes and ownership relationships. Retained v2 plans produce v8 from v7; retained v1 plans produce v7 from v6. Preview and apply a separate plan after each predecessor step until the executable reports current authority. Preserve the original plan and backup bytes, and never reinterpret an old plan as a current advancement. A failed or interrupted apply resumes with that same ID after inspecting its reported effects.

To reverse unchanged schema-migrated data, preview `pinboard migrate-schema --reverse <forward-plan-id>` at the same selected real root and apply its returned reverse ID. A later ledger write refuses reversal without changing authority; preserve the ledger and exact backup for diagnosis. Existing root-relocation backups, plans, progress, sidecars, aliases and Git exclusions remain historical data until a separate human disposition. They supply no operational recovery route.

Use these nonterminal states:

- `intake`: admitted but not yet ready for selection;
- `ready`: eligible for activation;
- `active`: one current execution attempt for that item; several disjoint items may be active concurrently;
- `paused`: preserved active attempt intentionally stopped mid-implementation;
- `blocked`: waiting for named work, evidence, or a decision;
- `deferred`: deliberately unscheduled with a concrete reopen condition;
- `review`: a frozen attempt awaiting independent acceptance.

All nonterminal states—including `ready`, `active`, and `review`—and their accepted briefs, candidate snapshots, and review evidence already persist durably on disk in `.pinboard/state.sqlite3` and `.pinboard/artifacts/` across sessions, models, and runtimes. Reserve `pause` for genuine mid-implementation stops in `active` rather than saving state, switching sessions or models, or holding a reviewed PR. Terminal state remains queryable as history and does not appear as live work.

## Leases and revocation

Project transitions are direct atomic SQLite changes made by a trusted local task. The supplied task and host strings are audit attribution, not authenticated credentials. Project transitions do not acquire or retain a project-wide lease. During contention, one exact transition commits completely or the prior revision remains; stale actions must be refreshed rather than replayed.

When `--json` returns `pinboard-rejected-operation/v1`, decide recovery from its effect facts before reading the message. `state_changed: false` means the failed invocation changed no Pinboard surface. `status: committed-effect` means the listed immutable artifact, accepted artifact reference, or ledger surface already changed; do not replay it. Use a returned action receipt only as one fresh same-subject alternative, copying its non-null lease and generation together. If no bounded alternative is returned, reacquire or reselect through the contract's named operation rather than inventing authority.

Attempt ownership is renewable and fenced. A worker presents its current attempt lease for item-local transitions. Replacing the attempt owner fences actions retained by the previous owner.

Use forced revocation only with explicit user authority when the recorded holder cannot release or has demonstrably abandoned the lease. Revocation increments the fencing generation. Never infer ownership from task titles, pinning, recency, or semantic similarity.

## Invalid state

When `pinboard validate --json` fails, report a compact recovery packet:

- the diagnostic codes and exact affected SQLite or artifact paths;
- whether the failure is authority, accepted-artifact, or generated-view state;
- the safest supported action that does not guess intent;
- one human question only when intent, scope, or product meaning is missing.

A `VIEW_REFRESH_REQUIRED` warning does not invalidate SQLite authority. Rebuild generated views only when the user authorizes that write or the active attempt requires it.

Do not edit SQLite directly or weaken validation. Recovery beyond initialization from absent `state.sqlite3` is not a general supported command. Preserve the observed failure and return it to the owning implementation when the executable cannot reopen the current database atomically.

## Interrupted tasks

A missing chat receipt is not evidence that a transition failed or succeeded. Never replay a retained action token.

For a task interrupted around a mutation:

1. Run `pinboard validate --json`.
2. Call `pinboard_item_status` operation `item` with exact project and work roots and the intended item. Compare its recorded state with the intended transition; absence from the live overview does not establish a terminal outcome. If the intended item still has its prior state, no transition committed. If it has the intended next state, the SQLite transition committed completely even if the task stopped before reporting it.
3. For an interrupted project transition, select the exact action again from current state and continue only if its semantics and payload are unchanged.
4. For interrupted preparation or attempt work, inspect the corresponding authority `status` and current item state. Continue a supplied same-worker lease only after validating its exact holder and generation. Use preparation `start` only while the item is ready; a paused item continues its existing attempt through the legal resume path, with replacement brief and rebind first if its accepted scope or Git lineage is stale. Use attempt `acquire` with the worker's own task and host when that resumed continuation calls for it. These ownership operations select initial ownership or a permissible inactive transfer under lock; neither tool exposes a `transfer` leaf. A live conflicting holder rejects unchanged. A higher generation fences actions retained by the interrupted task.
5. Use forced lease revocation only with explicit user authority when the recorded holder cannot release it or has demonstrably abandoned it.
6. Resume from the authoritative item and attempt state. Never reconstruct ownership from the stopped task's prose, generated views, archived files, or temporary payloads.

The observable transaction contract remains binary: the previous valid revision or one complete new revision. Report any counterexample as a current SQLite defect rather than routing around it.

## Inherited sessions

A session can inherit saved work from another session of the same runtime—for example a forked or resumed Codex thread, or a fresh session started after a long or drifted chat—or continue work after switching models (such as Sol to Opus) or runtimes. Because `ready`, `active`, and `review` states are already saved durably on disk, continuing in a fresh session or switching models or runtimes resumes directly from the recorded `ready`, `active`, or `review` state without pausing first; do not run `pause` or `return-for-correction` merely to save state, hand off a session, or hold a reviewed PR. When the human asks the inheriting or fresh session to continue that work and the original session is unavailable, meaning it ended, was closed, or cannot be reached from the current runtime, the inheriting session becomes the outcome owner. A recorded `owner_task_id` that names the original session is the attempt's activation provenance, not a routing gate; continuation needs no matching owner and no reassignment.

1. Obtain this session's own trusted task and host identity through the selected runtime instructions inline. Never reuse the original session's task or host from inherited conversation, generated views, or earlier tool arguments, and never present its retained receipts, leases, or worker handles as your own.
2. Treat inherited conversation as context, not state. Follow the [interrupted-task](#interrupted-tasks) steps from current authority: validate, read item status, inspect the named attempt, and follow its returned continuation.
3. Read preparation or attempt authority `status` before claiming work. An expired or released claim transfers through the ordinary `start` or `acquire` with this session's identity. A live claim held by the original session or one of its workers stays fenced: wait for it to lapse, or ask the human for forced revocation under [leases and revocation](#leases-and-revocation) when its holder demonstrably cannot release it.
4. The original session's native worker and reviewer handles are unavailable. Do not attempt same-worker continuation through them. When the continuation selects worker or review work, launch a fresh worker or reviewer from this session through the returned dispatch or review job.

While the original session remains available, it keeps outcome ownership. Continue there, or ask the human which session owns the work when both remain in use; inheriting the conversation alone does not move ownership.

Tell the human the outcome in plain words: whether you are continuing the earlier session's work or why you cannot yet, where its partial work lives and whether it reached the integration target, and the one decision you need, such as stopping the other window or overriding an unfinished worker that cannot be confirmed gone. Keep task identities, claims, leases, worker names and native handles out of the reply.

# Optional engineering-health baseline

Use this baseline only when the accepted item or canonical work brief explicitly selects it. A task looking complex, crossing several modules, or benefiting from more assurance is not enough. The accepted brief still owns the exact contract and mandatory verification; this reference does not create either.

## Close one representative contract

Before expanding a cross-boundary behavior across sibling variants, choose the cheapest supported value that can disprove agreement between the production owners and its real consumer.

1. Name the representative value, the observable consumer effect, and the production path between them.
2. Exercise that path through the application-owned boundary instead of proving each layer from separately constructed fixtures. When the path persists state, write it through the production operation and reload it from a fresh store before observing the consumer.
3. Put runtime evidence at the first real boundary capable of exposing disagreement: deserialization, persistence, an external system, an untyped value, relational state, or concurrency.
4. Expand sibling variants only after the representative path succeeds. Re-run the proof when a changed owner or representation can invalidate it.

The proof should be the smallest integration evidence that can falsify the contract. It is not a request for an exhaustive end-to-end suite.

## Count static guarantees fairly

Use concrete types, nominal identifiers, closed unions, exhaustive matching, and strict type-checker results as evidence for states supported code cannot construct. Do not add malformed domain objects, duplicate runtime guards, or tests solely to execute a statically unreachable branch.

Static evidence does not replace runtime evidence where values enter from deserialization, storage, external systems, untyped or cast boundaries, relational state, or concurrency.

## Treat repeated contradictions as architecture evidence

Correct a first representation mismatch at the owner that violated the contract, then rerun the representative proof. If the same boundary repeatedly produces incompatible representations after focused corrections, stop sibling expansion and return the contradiction to the accepted architecture or product owner. Do not normalize away facts in an adapter, multiply defensive review cases, or add downstream guards merely to keep the current path green.

Record the representative value, production path, static guarantees used, runtime boundary evidence, and outcome in the existing result and review evidence. Do not create a parallel artifact or schema.

## Stop at the baseline

The baseline is satisfied when the representative path succeeds, its owners agree on one supported representation, and no repeated contradiction remains unresolved. It does not add:

- complexity metrics, thresholds, or recovery automation;
- a cumulative architecture-fitness checkpoint;
- pre-execution architecture-decision compression;
- a generic architecture checklist;
- new ownership for architecture-impact declarations or closed-union recovery.

Those concerns require their own accepted scope and reopen evidence.

# Coding-agent runtime adapters


Pinboard exposes one SQLite authority, action vocabulary and brief schema through MCP and retained CLI operations. This document contains the shared workflow and selected runtime instructions inline. It grants no authority or permissions.


`<launcher-root>` is the resolved directory containing `scripts/pinboard`. Ordinary MCP declarations invoke that launcher with exactly `--mcp`; runtime hooks use their exact selectors described in their runtime's reference, and direct CLI operations use CLI arguments. CLI capture accepts only normal CLI targets and cannot wrap either protocol startup path. A caller may instead start one dedicated captured MCP process with the complete explicit pair described below. When `<launcher-root>` is a prepared `<pinboard-source>` checkout, the launcher uses `<pinboard-source>/.venv`. When it is an installed plugin version, the launcher uses `<launcher-root>/.pinboard-runtime/environment`. `<managed-project>` and its exact work root are request data, never runtime or dependency locations. Runtime selection follows the resolved launcher root, not the human or agent audience.


## Handling another runtime's attempt


A board is shared, so an agent in one runtime may coordinate, review, recover or reconcile an attempt that a worker in another runtime started. Use the attempt's recorded checkout facts (its `project_root`, branch, base revision and shared work root) and Pinboard tools for that attempt. Never use the other runtime's native handles, such as its task names, agent IDs or conversation IDs, and never follow its runtime reference for your own actions: native continuation, stop and wait apply only to workers your own runtime launched. When the other runtime's worker must be stopped or continued, report that to the human or its owning task instead.


## Public contracts and source scope


When Pinboard coordinates another project, use its advertised tools, verified artifacts and loaded public skill contracts. Its installed implementation, tests, private modules, generated code and database internals are outside that assignment; do not inspect them to derive protocol behavior, canonicalization or missing values. Pinboard source inspection remains available when the accepted assignment explicitly covers Pinboard development or a separate human-authorized Pinboard investigation.


If a required value or capability is unavailable, stop the affected operation before its dependent publication, lifecycle change or implementation. Preserve the exact project/work roots, accepted artifact identity and checkpoint when known; name the missing field or tool, the attempted operation and its consequence. Report observed target and auxiliary effects separately, or state that they are unknown; a missing input never proves that earlier calls had no effects. Use the exact supported recovery from the producing response or public contract. If none supplies the input, report that gap and the complete structured error to the human or owning coordinator. Resume only when a supported tool, verified artifact or documented contract supplies it. Do not invent, approximate or omit values, weaken independent judgment, reconstruct undocumented hashes, or use another agent, process or client as a proxy.


## Packaged connection and first setup


Each runtime's own reference names its packaged MCP declaration. Every declaration starts the existing `pinboard-mcp` entry through the same runtime owner. Ordinary declarations accept no additional arguments, and every tool call carries exact project and work roots. For an explicitly approved exact-evidence run, start a separate process as `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard --mcp --capture-evidence-dir <existing-directory> --safe-to-persist-exactly`. The selected directory applies only to that process; startup proves writable immutable publication before accepting callbacks, and partial declarations reject before startup without altering the installed manifests.


Resolve those roots before the first call. The project root is the exact selected checkout. Unless the user or an existing Pinboard receipt selected another work root, a normal checkout uses `<project-root>/.pinboard`. Read the exact selected initialized root; an unavailable root supplies no authority to choose another location. Explicit work roots retain their ordinary resolution and initialization rules. A released v6 ledger uses `migrate-schema` preview and apply at its selected real root while quiescent. A containing temporary directory, fixture root, checkout parent, or project root itself is not the work root. A linked worktree reuses only the exact shared work root supplied by its accepted workflow or resolved through the retained root command; do not guess it from the worktree path.


If a version is unprepared and uv is available, MCP startup invokes the same `--prepare-runtime` path and starts the server after readiness is verified. A runtime's SessionStart hook can also invoke that preparation; the version-local lock serializes both callers. Missing uv, contention or failed preparation leaves the MCP connection attempt unavailable and puts its strict same-launcher recovery on stderr, never protocol stdout. The hook reports its own preparation facts and the exact manual command as additional context; it cannot establish the current connection status. Deliberate CLI setup may run `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard --prepare-runtime` with uv and write access only to that version's `.pinboard-runtime`. Follow the exact preparation result and check tool availability. Use the client's supported MCP reconnect or plugin reload mechanism if the connection remains unavailable after preparation. Setup and CLI-only operations retain their direct launcher route. A missing required MCP tool stops that operation and never authorizes shell fallback.


MCP initialization directs each launched role to its verified envelope’s selected startup document. A coordinator or intake caller uses the coordinator document for its current runtime before attributed calls. Do not replace an already selected role with coordinator startup.


Pinboard wire identities, such as intake's `pinboard_overview` and `pinboard_proposal_create`, identify the required operations. The current host may advertise different full callable names for them. Resolve the native name before selecting a deferred tool schema:


1. Find the required operation in the host's actual tool announcement or native inventory and copy its full callable name, including the connector prefix. Resolve each host's names independently.
2. When the full name is known, use the host's exact-name selection with that full name. When it is unresolved, use supported keyword discovery to find the advertised callable.
3. If exact selection returns no match, reconcile the selected name with the actual advertised inventory. When a short wire name was selected, retry with the advertised full callable name. An unmatched short-name selection or an incomplete broad search does not establish a missing connection.
4. Inspect the returned callable identity and schema against the required operation, then invoke that native callable with exact project and work roots under its negotiated contract.


Do not infer that subagents are unavailable because an unrelated, nested, shell, MCP, or dynamically listed tool surface omits their controls. Report a missing subagent capability only after the runtime's native launch surface is actually absent or unsupported, or an actual required native launch returns an unavailable or unsupported result.


No adapter authorizes one client to control another or use another client's connection as a fallback.


## Current MCP request shapes


The native tools share one installed surface. These tools carry their exact selected leaf inside one strict `request` object: `pinboard_brief_contract`, `pinboard_brief_sources`, `pinboard_fixture_review`, `pinboard_startup_text`, `pinboard_brief_source_plan_output`, `pinboard_item_definition`, `pinboard_obligation_coverage`, `pinboard_item_status`, `pinboard_brief_review`, `pinboard_pr_review`, `pinboard_order`, `pinboard_parallel_preview`, `pinboard_actions`, `pinboard_preparation_authority`, `pinboard_attempt_authority`, `pinboard_transition`, `pinboard_cancel`, and `pinboard_initiative`. For attempt status, use `{"request": {"project_root": "<exact checkout>", "work_root": "<exact work root>", "operation": "status", "attempt_id": "<exact attempt>"}}`. The roots, role or operation, and selected leaf fields all belong inside `request`. Unknown outer or inner fields and flat calls are rejected unchanged. The remaining tools retain their advertised ordinary object arguments. Discover and follow each current negotiated schema rather than copying a historical call.


`pinboard_close` is one of those remaining tools and has a single project role, so it takes no `request` wrapper and no `role`: `{"project_root": "<exact checkout>", "work_root": "<exact work root>", "receipt": {"action_id": {"kind": "close", "subject": "<item>"}, "subject_revision": "<from pinboard_actions>"}, "payload": {"outcome": "done", "reason": "<one line>", "human_decision": "<the human's explicit close decision in their own words>"}, "actor_task_id": "<task>", "actor_host_id": "<host>"}`. `human_decision` is required, nonempty and single-line; without the human's own words, ask the human and stop rather than writing them. Whether the human is asked to confirm each close depends on the runtime; its own reference says how. Report a denied close to the human and seek no other route. `pinboard_transition` has no close leaf and refuses a close receipt unchanged, naming `pinboard_close`.


Use `pinboard_item_status` with `{"request": {"project_root": "<exact checkout>", "work_root": "<exact work root>", "operation": "item", "item_id": "<exact item>"}}` for one item's `pinboard-item-status/v5` result: state, labeled intake-time `intake_context`, the current attempt with its `branch`, `pause_reason` and `current_checkpoint` (`continue` with `checkpoint_id`, `title` and exact `remaining_work`, `terminal` with `checkpoint_id` and `title`, or `unreadable` with a `message`), full dependency reasons, proposal origin and planned replacement, the current attempt's `review_verdict` (`none`, `returned-for-correction`, `ready`, `accepted-and-continued`, or `checkpoint-accepted`), a terminal item's `closure` with its closing action, committed time, and, for a completion, closing attempt, and `board` with the absolute `markdown` and `html` paths of the generated board page under the selected work root, named whether or not those files exist yet. Use operation `branch` with an exact `branch` instead of `item_id` for `pinboard-branch-owners/v1`, which lists every item and attempt that recorded that branch. Use operation `integration` with an exact `item_id` and `target` (a local branch, remote-tracking ref, tag, or full commit id; Pinboard never fetches) for `pinboard-item-integration/v1`, which names the target's resolved `target_revision`, the reviewed candidate `source` (`protected-review`, `accepted-checkpoint` with its `checkpoint`, or `completion`) with its `compared_from_revision`, and `presence`: `content-present`, `content-not-present`, or `no-change`. All three leaves reject through `pinboard-mcp-item-status-result/v3`; the integration leaf adds `INTEGRATION_TARGET_UNRESOLVED`, `INTEGRATION_CANDIDATE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INTEGRATION_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_INVALID`, and an unchanged Git-checkout rejection carrying its `PROJECT_GIT_*` code; `BRANCH_OWNER_NOT_FOUND` also covers a branch recorded before a rebind, and `TRANSITION_RECEIPT_DAMAGED` names a consumed receipt whose outcome does not decode, with a diagnosis-only recovery: `pinboard validate` for a pause or paused-rebind receipt, otherwise a report of the named receipt and defect to the human.


`pinboard_dispatch` takes ordinary `project_root`, `work_root` and one strict `dispatch` leaf, without a `request` wrapper. Its registration description makes the six inline worker-launch leaves, separate replacement-readiness leaf and their declared file counterparts, their exact common fields and distinct review inputs explicit when a host loses construction details in callable metadata. The negotiated schema and typed decoder remain authoritative; this description does not repair the host's schema translator. Use only `action_id` and `subject_revision` from the fresh project dispatch action for `receipt`, and explicit `prompt: null` for canonical construction. Action discovery omits `payload_schema` for dispatch because no lifecycle-transition payload applies; construct its separate request through `pinboard_dispatch`. Ordinary and reviewed construction serve initial work. `local-correction` takes a local review bound to the accepted brief and an independent reviewer; `correction` retains the effective cross-boundary contract review. `reuse-correction` carries a fresh independent candidate-bound assessment and reuses accepted ready coverage only while the accepted brief and every reviewed source remain exact. All correction leaves bind the current return receipt, accepted starting snapshot, and exact reason. Initial ready review alone cannot substitute for candidate-bound correction review.


`pinboard_correction_context` takes ordinary exact `project_root`, `work_root`, `attempt_id`, and `correction_history_id` arguments. Its read-only `pinboard-correction-context/v2` result returns the complete effective correction brief, exact brief/checkpoint/authority-set hashes, canonical return reason, accepted starting candidate identity, exact `starting_candidate_reference`, executable `starting_candidate_verification` arguments for `pinboard_artifact_verify`, typed `starting_snapshot_metadata`, and advisory `reuse_eligible` and `reuse_blockers`. Use it before independent correction-source review and follow [complete snapshot inspection](#prepare-and-publish-review-evidence) before assessing the candidate. Dispatch rechecks current source, accepted ready review, and snapshot identity after review; the read alone grants no authority and cannot freeze the checkout.


`pinboard_return_context` takes ordinary exact roots, `attempt_id`, and a strict `selection` with `kind: historical` or `kind: current-candidate` and the caller-selected `return_history_id`. Its `pinboard-return-context/v2` historical selection returns the exact original canonical return receipt, verified starting-candidate identity, and the same exact accepted snapshot reference, verification arguments and typed metadata as correction context, after rebind or rebase and while a later pause or protected review leaves the selected return historical. It decodes and verifies only the selected receipt/snapshot evidence and grants no current correction authority. Finding the original submission may traverse unrelated revision-index entries between submission and return under the current schema; lookup work grows with those intervening receipts. This accepted limitation also affects the shared correction/replacement recovery reader; reopen when focused recovery becomes noticeably slow. No project export or full validation is required. Current-candidate selection additionally requires the current active return and the returned branch, HEAD and accepted base; it supplies plain effective review evidence plus the current tracked candidate and sorted omitted untracked path names. Untracked bytes remain outside candidate identity. Both selections require [complete snapshot inspection](#prepare-and-publish-review-evidence); the compact result supplies provenance rather than an independent assessment. Independently assess that complete subject before `candidate-correction` dispatch. Its `brief_review` is `pinboard-current-correction-source-review/v1`, with `boundary: cross-boundary` and a full `CorrectionSourceReview` as `source_review`, or `boundary: local` and a `LocalCorrectionSourceReview`; both carry the exact observed `current_candidate` binding. Existing exact-checkout correction and coverage-reuse shapes remain available. The read publishes nothing, and dispatch repeats current-return, historical-snapshot, lineage, candidate/path and source checks around publication.


`pinboard_candidate_restore` takes ordinary object arguments: exact `project_root`, `work_root`, `attempt_id`, and inspected `candidate`. Candidate recovery returns a native `restore` invocation with the chosen work root and exact candidate preserved; `project_root: null` is explicitly unresolved. Supply the caller-selected exact clean checkout on the recorded branch and preimage before invoking it. The tool restores only the current accepted snapshot context, not arbitrary archived checkpoints; an inspected candidate superseded by a newer submission rejects before Git. Source effects finish after entry and report only actual `source-checkout` changes or a committed post-mutation failure with `do-not-retry`. Restoration acquires no authority, changes no ledger or lifecycle, creates no checkout and launches no task.


`pinboard_attempt_inspect` takes ordinary exact roots, `attempt_id`, and required nullable `reconciliation`. Pass `null` for ordinary inspection. For a favorably reviewed candidate, `null` returns an ordinary review-state continuation of kind `reconcile-repository` that names the reviewed candidate and the repository reconciliation needed next; it is not a failed read. Then pass the outer coordinator's nonempty target revision, exact integration relation, legal repository phase, and exactly three effect observations in source-checkout, shared-work-root, git-metadata order to select one repository continuation. The adapter observes those repository and permission facts and performs only the returned continuation; Pinboard does not grant permissions or run Git, checkout, shared-work-root, cleanup, disposition, or terminal effects. A paused continuation carries `pause_reason`: the reason recorded by the current pause, carried forward by a paused rebind, or `null` for a checkpoint pause or an unrecorded reason. `pinboard_item_status` reports the same `pause_reason` on its current attempt.


`pinboard_review_job` takes exact roots and one `review` leaf. Ordinary `initial`, `package-initial`, `correction`, and `package-correction` remain repair-free and reject before prompt publication when the exact current candidate already has a valid ready-review record. Caller-selected retired v1/v2 checkpoint packages reject unchanged before publication. Their verified terminal archives preserve exact readable history and incoming completion coverage, but cannot authorize review, correction or restoration. Current v3 packages require their exact accepted candidate evidence and independent closure, including original brief and ready-review bindings; an archive waives none of those checks. Run full validation separately before selecting package evidence. The `record-ready` leaf is separate: it requires exact current candidate, snapshot, accepted-brief, result and review digests, `reviewer_prompt_sha256` copied from the `prompt_reference.sha256` that a launch leaf returned for that exact candidate, brief and `result.md`, the identity of the reviewer launched from that prompt, `verdict: ready`, and nonempty acceptance evidence. It takes no runtime or background fields, never launches a reviewer, and returns only the canonical `pinboard-candidate-review/v2` record and exact publication accounting. A digest that names no reviewer prompt published for that subject—a missing, worker, foreign or older-result prompt—rejects unchanged with `REVIEWER_PROMPT_NOT_COMMISSIONED`; run the review job for the current candidate first. Terminal completion through either payload leaf rejects unchanged with `CANDIDATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` until such a recorded review names the completion's `reviewer_task_id`; its observations name the missing exact review binding and one read-only attempt inspection. The closure refusal does not commission or launch a reviewer.


`pinboard_order` takes exact roots, the existing strict `order` record (`schema: pinboard-live-order/v1`, complete `expected_order` and authorized `requested_order`) and trusted `actor_task_id`/`actor_host_id` inside `request`. It needs no preparation or worker lease and grants no launch authority. Its result preserves the committed receipt or unchanged rejection; known committed warnings name the exact retained CLI view-repair command. The structured `recovery` starts bounded `pinboard_overview` traversal (`max_items: 25`, `continuation: null`) for current-state reconciliation; follow every returned continuation at the same revision before reconstructing complete order. This is not proof that this caller committed or recovery of its lost receipt. Equal order after a valid no-op cannot distinguish a committed call from one that never ran. There is no exactly-once guarantee; never blindly replay a lost reply or committed warning.


`pinboard_parallel_preview` takes exact roots and `selection: selected` with nonempty unique supported `item_ids`, or explicit `selection: all-safe` without item IDs, inside `request`. Selected reads focused current facts; all-safe reads current portfolio constraints without proposal bodies or retained history. Neither leaf changes artifacts, views, lifecycle, authority or native tasks. Structural safety does not certify readiness or replace human batch permission and fresh launch checks.


Use `pinboard_item_definition` operation `current` with exact roots and `item_id` for the complete accepted definition and its current identity. Its `history` leaf additionally requires an explicit `limit` from 1 to 100 and `before_revision`: begin with `null`, then use the returned `next_before_revision` as the exclusive cursor while it is non-null. Both leaves are read-only and require no lease.


Use `pinboard_brief_review` operation `publish` with exact roots, `brief_artifact_ref_id`, and a complete structured `pinboard-work-brief-review-needs-correction/v1` record bound to that accepted brief. The `status` leaf takes roots and the exact reference only; it verifies the accepted bytes and returns the canonical brief, `accepted_brief_sha256`, `checkpoint_sha256`, `reviewed_authority_set_sha256`, and verified latest negative evidence, if any. Both status variants carry the same bindings: copy them for initial ready or negative review; the accepted-brief digest equals `accepted_brief.sha256`, and the other digests use the existing canonical checkpoint and ordered-authority codec. These facts establish the review subject, never the review conclusion. Corrupt or unreadable accepted bytes return `ARTIFACT_BYTES_INVALID` with unchanged target effects and `do-not-retry`; preserve the named resource for human diagnosis. Wrap returned `correction.status_request` inside `request` when calling the same tool. The correction target names `pinboard_brief_publish` and its exact roots; add the complete corrected brief as `brief`. Neither negative evidence nor its absence proves ready review, changes lifecycle, or acquires authority.


Focused project `pinboard_actions` discovery for the exact `complete` action supplies the current completion contract. When closure lacks a protected current candidate or the accepted checkpoint still continues, that focused MCP result reports the pending condition, includes the exact accepted `remaining_work` for a continuing checkpoint, and supplies one read-only `pinboard_attempt_inspect` input with the caller's exact roots. Follow the inspection to establish what remains before choosing further authorized work. Discovery supplies no acquisition, submission, dispatch or scope-replacement recipe and never reconstructs a candidate automatically.


Historical definition queries and portable export preserve the original v1 schema and full fields without a checkout policy or synthesized obligations. These records are historical evidence, never current execution authority. Activation, rebind, resume and dispatch require a genuine current supported definition: origin-free v2 or origin-bearing v3.


`pinboard_cancel` accepts one strict top-level `request` containing the `preview` or `confirm` operation and exact project/work roots. Preview requires `item_id`. Confirm additionally requires the preview's exact `binding`, the separate human reply as `human_confirmation`, and trusted current `actor_task_id` and `actor_host_id`. The preview token and quoted words do not authenticate human authorship. Follow the [separate chat confirmation procedure](#cancel-after-separate-exact-item-confirmation); generic transitions accept no cancellation leaf.


### Verified record file inputs


For a completed brief or independent review too large to transmit reliably inline, write that one complete JSON record to an exact caller-selected file with ordinary file tools, hash its raw bytes, and invoke only the corresponding advertised file input below. This is the sole record-file exception to the no-temporary-payload rule. It never substitutes for a missing tool, manufactures identity or authority, or permits shell, Python or direct SQLite calls into Pinboard state. All small controls stay inline under the negotiated schema.


| Tool and file input | Selected record and controls |
| --- | --- |
| `pinboard_brief_publish_file` | Ordinary top-level `project_root`, `work_root`, `brief_path`, `brief_sha256`; file contains the complete current `WorkBrief`. |
| `pinboard_dispatch` kinds `reviewed-file`, `correction-file`, `reuse-correction-file`, `local-correction-file`, `candidate-correction-file`, `replacement-readiness-file` | Replace only `brief_review` with `brief_review_path` and `brief_review_sha256`. Keep every corresponding inline leaf's controls, including `current_candidate` for replacement readiness. Candidate correction's file contains the complete outer `CurrentCorrectionReview`, including `boundary`, `source_review` and `current_candidate`, for either boundary variant. |
| `pinboard_brief_review` operation `publish-file` | Inside `request`, retain roots and `brief_artifact_ref_id`; replace `review` with `review_path` and `review_sha256`. The file contains `WorkBriefReviewNeedsCorrection`. |
| `pinboard_pr_review` operations `start-file`, `review-brief-file`, `round-file` | Inside `request`, retain roots, item, expected revision and actor controls. Replace the corresponding `brief`, `brief_review` or `round` with `<field>_path` and `<field>_sha256`. The file contains that leaf's exact `ReviewBrief`, `BriefReview` or `ReviewRound`. |


The file SHA-256 binds the raw bytes, including whitespace. Pinboard reads those bytes once, verifies them, strictly decodes the exact record, then calls the existing publication owner. Accepted artifact digests continue to bind canonical output and may differ from the raw input digest. Inline forms remain supported; a valid digest changes no binding, freshness, independence, coverage, candidate or collision check, and establishes no authenticated authorship or readiness. Only the selected file is read and it is never changed by publication.


`INPUT_FILE_UNREADABLE` names the file and expected digest with the observed digest explicitly unavailable. `INPUT_FILE_DIGEST_MISMATCH` reports both digests. Both reject with unchanged target effects and a safe input-correction step; malformed records use the operation's ordinary decode rejection. After publication, honor actual effect, changed surfaces and retry disposition, including committed failures. Lost brief publication through either input form uses the exact brief-lookup recovery below; do not replay a possible committed effect.


## Brief construction and source preparation


Use `pinboard_brief_contract` with a strict `request` containing exact roots and `operation: full`, or `operation: starter` with `boundary: local` or `cross-boundary`. Copy the returned complete starter, choose its structural variants, and fill unresolved values from accepted facts. Construction resolves no roots or ledger and grants no readiness or authority.


Use read-only `pinboard_brief_sources` with exact roots inside `request`: `plan` takes a structured `manifest` and positive `max_batch_bytes`; `emit` takes the returned structured plan and nonnegative `batch_index`. The complete inline plan and each emitted batch must fit the presented-result limit. If a plan exceeds it, divide the manifest into smaller selections and use `plan` and `emit` for each without a write or human replanning. Read each verified batch once in order, and resume at the first unread `batch_index` from the same plan after an interruption. Use write-capable `pinboard_brief_source_plan_output` for `plan-to-file` only when a durable plan is explicitly needed, with one destination; then read batches through the read-only `emit-file` leaf using `plan_path` and `batch_index`. On Antigravity, any agent loading sources through a source plan—whether for brief preparation, brief review, worker delivery, or a status expansion—keeps `plan` or `plan-to-file` but reads the selected sources through the Antigravity native-source procedure with native `read_file` instead of `emit` or `emit-file` (where brief and worker reads retain `pinboard_dispatch`'s reviewed-authority digest check and status-expansion source plans have neither read-time `emit` verification nor a subsequent `pinboard_dispatch` check); the per-batch presented-result limit then applies only to the plan. Planning and emission resolve the selected source checkout and never open work state. Plan-to-file creates or identically reuses only its exact immutable destination; a differing destination rejects unchanged. A visible output followed by synchronization failure reports committed `selected-output` and `do-not-retry`; inspect that destination, never replay the failure. Required roots are context, not permission to create durable state.


### Recover a lost brief-publication result


When `pinboard_brief_publish` or `pinboard_brief_publish_file` may have committed but its result was lost, recover with `pinboard_brief_lookup` using ordinary arguments `project_root`, `work_root`, `attempt_id` and positive `artifact_revision` from the original brief record. Do not replay publication. The read selects only that exact accepted brief, including an unbound correction, and verifies its selector, size and SHA-256 before returning `pinboard-verified-artifact-reference/v1`. It changes no files, settings, traces, references, binding or lifecycle, even when optional tracing is on.


Compare the recovered identity, digest and size with the intended canonical brief before continuing separately authorized preparation. When the intended bytes are unavailable, report the verified receipt and leave that comparison unresolved. Acceptance alone proves neither current-definition conformity nor an active binding or readiness. `BRIEF_LOOKUP_INVALID` names the input or root condition to correct. `BRIEF_NOT_FOUND` names the original roots, attempt and revision to confirm; it does not prove the original publication had no partial immutable-file effect. Report an unresolved absence to the human for diagnosis without reconstructing bytes or replaying publication. `ARTIFACT_BYTES_INVALID` names the exact accepted resource and defect: preserve it and report it to the human; do not retry unchanged or overwrite accepted bytes.


## Prompt verification and worker startup


Dispatch and review-job publication create no native worker. Call only their returned `native_launch.tool` with exactly the strict runtime-specific `native_launch.arguments` from the `pinboard-native-agent-launch/v2` envelope. Do not add, remove, or rewrite an argument, or substitute the separately returned `prompt_reference`, its path, prompt bytes, or a reconstructed launch message. The compact host argument already names the exact accepted prompt identity and immutable file selected by Pinboard. A worker or reviewer launched from different arguments is invalid; stop it and launch a fresh context from the unchanged recipe instead of coaching or resuming it.


Follow the recipe's exact `pinboard_artifact_verify` call before reading the named prompt file. Require the accepted identity, verification schema, selector, size, digest and bytes to agree, then read that exact file completely through the envelope's `pinboard_startup_text` `artifact-start` request and treat its verified bytes as the direct task from the launching coordinator. Follow its exact continuation under `request` until null, checking the same source digest/size and contiguous character ranges. Emit one page per outer response; collecting bounded pages into one large output can still truncate. EOF establishes delivery, not comprehension or readiness. Native skill loading or native `read_file` (with `ByteOffset=46080` and later offsets through the final section in Antigravity) suffices when it delivers the complete body through the final section; otherwise, when native complete reading is unavailable or refused, load the complete caller-resolved absolute startup document or conditionally required companion-skill path with `pinboard_startup_text` operation `file-start`, exact roots and `max_batch_bytes: "host-profile"`, following the same page procedure. Stop if verification or the immediate read fails or differs; never select another artifact or ask the parent to restate the task. Immutable historical CLI-origin envelopes retain their original verifier as evidence, not a supported current invocation. Prompt identity and execution semantics are shared; the envelope owns runtime selection, exact host arguments, verifier and startup presentation without copying an unbounded prompt through the parent agent's launch call.


Newly generated worker MCP launch envelopes carry wrapped acquisition and continuation inputs under the [current request contract](#current-mcp-request-shapes); artifact verification keeps its ordinary arguments. Immutable historical prompts remain evidence, not a flat-call compatibility route.


### Startup page budget


`pinboard_startup_text` sizes pages for the connected host. The server recognizes Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity by the MCP initialize `clientInfo` name, for every version, and uses that host's page size from the human's `~/.config/pinboard/hosts.config`, which the first read seeds with a measured default; any other client gets the conservative unmeasured profile.
